# PRI breathing exercise selection

Full source: `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-breathing-exercise-selection.txt` (Ryne Gioviano, *PRI Foundations for the Strength Coach*).

## Core idea
Humans are asymmetrical. Fix pelvis/ribcage position **before** loading. Breathing/PRI sits early in the warm-up so we don't squat a flared, extended frame.

## Patterns to recognize
- **Left AIC:** left hemi-pelvis anterior/forward, mass on right; hard to shift into left AF IR. Look for right foot turn-out, right-biased stance, limited left adduction drop.
- **Right BC:** right lat / apical restriction; limited left trunk rotation/sidebend; common in swimmers with overworked lats.
- **PEC:** bilateral extension bias; limited trunk rotation both ways; hard toe-touch / SLR.

Red flags (inform warm-up/tertiary, don't diagnose): can't toe-touch, heels-up squat, SLR <90°, limited shoulder IR, limited trunk rotation, left adduction drop fail, obvious right weight shift.

## Repositioning menu (coach these)
| Exercise | Objective |
|---|---|
| 90/90 Hip Lift w/ Balloon | Inhibit Left AIC, restore ZOA, inhibit Right BC/lat |
| Left Sidelying Left Flexed Adduction | Left IC adductor + right abductor (frontal plane) |
| Retro Stairs | Left glute med / Left AF IR |
| Standing Resisted Wall Reach | Serratus, thoracic flexion, lat inhibition |

Still generally **one** athlete-specific technique at warm-up and end of session (same drill). Very patterned or in-pain athletes may get a second warm-up-only drill.

### Standing Serratus Squat vs Standing Wall Press with L PME
Pick from Postural Respiration lists - do not paraphrase as "stiff mid-back."

- **Standing Serratus Squat** (Anterior Neck Inhibition list, p.76; also filed under L LT/L Serratus and L PME): forward head, neck that won't relax on reaches, limited horizontal abduction or cervical rotation. Script (appendix p.18): face wall, elbows at shoulder height bent 90°, press elbows into wall, round/tuck, squat until knees touch the wall, heels down, 4-5 breaths filling the upper back ×5.
- **Standing Wall Press with Left Posterior Mediastinum Expansion** (Left Posterior Mediastinum list, p.77): limited right trunk rotation, limited right apical expansion, limited left shoulder horizontal abduction, or difficulty with the Posterior Mediastinum Respiratory Reach Test. Script (appendix p.36): hands on wall, 1-2 inch block or towel under the **left** hand, maximally round, inhale while gently pressing and fill the **left** upper back, 4-5 breaths ×5.
- The "very stiff/rigid back" / forward locomotion without rib rotation line belongs to the **p.75 PEC Paravertebral** list (Squatting Bar Reach, Heel Stair Descents, etc.), not the Wall Press indication.
- Platt rule of thumb (appendix p.52): right intercostal work ≈ frontal plane; left posterior mediastinum ≈ transverse plane.

## Squat breathing variations
1. Partial exhale down, full exhale up - weaker abs / heavier loads
2. Exhale down, hold 1-3 breaths at bottom, exhale up - extension breathers / PEC-Right BC
3. Inhale down, exhale up - earned; established ZOA only

Detail and Left AIC/PEC rationale: open [PRI The Squat and Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-squat-and-respiration).

## Programming link
- Pair extension-heavy strength with a flexion/reach or breathing check (e.g. trap-bar + serratus/child's-pose breathing).
- Swimmers: every program needs some squat-and-reach / wall-reach work, lat inhibition, serratus + subscap focus - not cuff isolation alone.
- Success isn't only bar weight; can they keep neutrality (toe-touch / SLR) after training?
- Lift order after restoration gates: [Fitness and Movement](sand-workflow:fitness-and-movement).

## Deep PRI course references (open when …)

Use this skill for day-of Achieve breathing/tertiary picks. Open the matching skill when you need expert-level discussion, test interpretation, inhibit/facilitate tables, hierarchies, or decision trees:

| Open | When |
|---|---|
| [PRI Myokinematic Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-myokinematic-restoration) | Lumbo-pelvic-femoral / AF-FA Left AIC; ADT, EDT, SLR, FA ROM, Hruska Adduction/Abduction Lifts; AF IR "real estate"; glute max / IC adductor / hamstring facilitation. Gate: **− ADT / − PADT** stays Myokinematic. |
| [PRI Pelvis Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-pelvis-restoration) | Pelvic inlet/outlet, pelvic diaphragm, PADT/PART, PEC vs Patho PEC, IS instability, hemibridge/adductor pull-back/wall-reach course selection. Gate: **− ADT / + PADT** (or bilateral −/+ ) → Pelvis. |
| [PRI Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) | ZOA, Right BC, PEC thorax, apical expansion, lat/intercostal/paraspinal inhibition, neuromotor order overview. |
| [PRI Right BC Treatment Guidelines](sand-workflow:pri-right-bc-treatment-guidelines) | Right BC **test cluster + decision tree**: when to progress R low trap/tricep vs L low trap/serratus vs R serratus vs R subscap; Superior T4 / Subclavius / Infraclavicular clinician paths; ZOA NM entry list. |
| [PRI The Squat and Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-squat-and-respiration) | Squat descent/ascent breathing variants; when inhale-on-descent is earned; Left AIC / PEC pelvic-rib setup under load. |
| [PRI Swimming An In-Depth Look](sand-workflow:pri-swimming-in-depth) | PRI swim pattern (PEC + L AIC/R BC), stroke pathomechanics, dryland implications (freestyle/fly/back/breast). Not pool ISO angles. |
| [PRI Primary Non-Manual Techniques Workshop](sand-workflow:pri-non-manual-techniques-workshop) | Technique selection, reference/referent cueing, position ladders, workshop technique cards. |
| [PRI Impingement and Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) | Positional vs primary impingement; multi-directional instability grading; calcaneal/knee/FA/HG/scapular-thoracic tables; subscapularis vs lat IR; secondary course after intros. |
| [Swim turn and start ISO angles](sand-workflow:swim-turn-and-start-iso-angles) | Pool-transfer ISO joint angles for flip/open turn or start (separate from PRI swim dryland skill). |

**Course chain:** Myokinematic (AF/FA) → Pelvis (inlet/outlet hold) → Postural Respiration (ZOA/thorax) → Right BC guidelines (thorax decision tree) → Impingement & Instability (joints that still impinge or go unstable).

# PRI Impingement & Instability (course skill)

**Source (full text):** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-impingement-instability.txt`  
*(OCR from scanned PDF - Prefer cross-checking exercise titles against Postural Respiration clean appendix when OCR is noisy. Host copy notes Achieve, June 2019.)*  
**Manual:** *Impingement & Instability* (PRI, © 2007-2019).  
**Course level:** Secondary / advanced relative to Myokinematic, Pelvis, and Postural Respiration intros.

---

## 1. Core theory / asymmetry model (this course)

### Positional impingement ≠ primary (shape) impingement
PRI definitions (manual "PRI Concepts of Impingement and Instability"):
- Impingement here is **not** attributed primarily to abnormalities of the shape of long bones/articulating surfaces.  
- It reflects **occult dynamic instability** from **malaligned structural position/orientation**.  
- It reflects **Left AIC and Right BC patterns of compensation**.  
- Assessed/addressed with PRI approaches. Symptoms can mimic primary impingement, but **positional impingement** is different. Traditional conservative/operative approaches aimed at assumed primary impingement often failed until the **patterned instability** (Left AIC/Right BC unilateral dominance, habit, consistent hand/foot usage) was addressed first - then impingement resolved secondarily.

### Instability framing (Position vs Primary table)
**Frequency**
- Acute - maintain neutral position  
- Recurrent - reposition and immediately address joint internal rotation  
- Chronic - after repositioning, maximize with **Right AIC / Left BC** tri-planar neuromotor strength and skills  

**Etiology:** atraumatic positional patterns → retrain opposition muscles of Left AIC/Right BC after repositioning (PRI non-manual or manual). Distinguish microtraumatic/repetitive, voluntary/involuntary, traumatic macro, congenital (primary column).

**Direction**
- Unidirectional - see PRI pathology table; **1 PRI test per girdle joint is negative**  
- Bidirectional - **2 PRI tests negative** per girdle joint in different planes  
- Multidirectional - **2+ PRI tests negative** per girdle joint in **2+ planes**  

**Degree:** subluxation refers to FA, HG, MT joints (vs dislocation on primary side). Patient volition: involuntary as produced by PRI examiner vs voluntary.

### Biomechanical treatment considerations of impingement (Position vs Primary)
Position column examples: capsular malalignment; proximal aligned control; compensatory bony impact secondary to unorganized triplanar unilateral overactivity; poor strength secondary to improper muscle attachment position; generated force from inappropriate muscle (dyssynchrony).  
Primary column: capsular stiffness; joint degeneration; malformation of arthrokinetic surfaces; weakness of antagonistic/agonistic force couples; poor timing (asynchrony).

### Pitfalls to stabilization rehabilitation (manual list)
Failure to address pain/hypomobility; failure to follow progression steps; failure to ensure proper patterns of movement; failure to ensure proper muscle firing sequences; allowing incorrect movement patterns; failure to understand mechanics of selected movements; failure to understand demands of patient's functional activities; failure to involve the whole (pattern), etc.

### Overview table - possible I&I associated with Left AIC / Right BC
Examples (RIGHT vs LEFT columns in manual):
- Hallux limitus (active R / passive L)  
- Ankle inversion sprains (R) vs talocalcaneal instability (L)  
- Anterior medial knee instability (R; ↑ valgum → lateral knee strain) vs lateral knee instability (L; ↑ varum → medial knee strain)  
- Anteromedial FA impingement (R) vs anterosuperior AF impingement (L)  
- Laterosuperior FA impingement / AF multidirectional instability themes  
- Ilio-sacral mechanical vs pathomechanic instability  
- Superior posterior humeral glenoid impingement; HG multidirectional instability; humeral acromial impingement  
- Thoracic-sternal instability; SLAP lesions (especially if full HG IR exists)  
- L4/L5/S1 instability notes  

Unilateral idiopathic indicators listed early: hip (AF or FA) impingement / iliosacral pain; posterior superior ilio-lateral (QL) "tightness"; ear fullness or preference.

---

## 2. Patterns to recognize (I&I lens)

### Left AIC / Right BC remains the patterned engine
I&I assumes the intro patterns. When neutrality is intermittent or tests go negative in multiple planes, joints express **impingement on the compressed side** and **instability on the unsupported side** of the same patterned system.

### Foot / ankle / calcaneal
Agenda: Left AIC foot and ankle pattern; PEC foot and ankle; calcaneal instability; frontal-plane calcaneal stability. Calcaneal eversion programs appear in snapping-hip / FA instability hierarchies when frontal-plane FA instability couples to calcaneus.

### Knee
Genu hyperextension instability; anterior medial vs lateral knee instability paired to Right vs Left pattern columns.

### Hip / groin / FA-AF
Hip and groin impingement lab; anteromedial FA vs anterosuperior AF; multidirectional FA instability; snapping hip syndrome (lateral FA instability secondary to long/weak glute med/min - femoral head migrates; often left; clicks with FA IR/ER more than AF).

### Ilio-sacral
Ilium stability depends on position/efficiency of iliacus, glute med/min, biceps femoris, adductor brevis, pectineus - stabilize ilium during contralateral swing; sagittal/frontal force closure for acetabulum-on-femur. Poor iliacus/pectineus-adductor position → reduced ilium stability; ground forces facilitate superior-posterior sacral advancement (ilio-sacral internal rotation) → unilateral lordosis themes (cross-ref Pelvis Restoration).

### Scapular-thoracic / HG
Scapula-thoracic instability; Hruska classification of scapular resting position; superior posterior HG impingement when patterned IR is forced (links to Postural Respiration Right BC humeral test position warning); multidirectional HG instability; need **subscapularis** for true HG IR after lat/pec pathways are inhibited.

### Right AIC / Left BC frontal-plane view
Manual includes Right AIC / Left BC posterior frontal-plane figures (left thoracic abduction / right thoracic adduction language) - the flip side after successful inhibition of Left AIC/Right BC, used when maximizing chronic instability rehab.

---

## 3. Assessment themes

I&I uses intro PRI tests as the language of "how many tests are negative per girdle joint / how many planes" to grade unidirectional vs multi-directional instability.

**Examples of clinical clusters (OCR treatment pages):**
- + Left ADT; decreased/limited Left FA IR; medial tibial plateau pain with medial footwear issues → orthotic/footwear notes; achieve bilateral Adduction and Abduction Lift scores ≥3; maximize Right AF ER; balance hamstrings with left medial hamstring focus; standing supported Left AF IR with right FA abduction integration.  
- Snapping hip test results themes: ↑ passive FA abduction; limited active FA abduction strength; ipsilateral Adduction Lift >3 / Abduction Lift findings → hierarchy below.  
- Right BC cluster after upright work: Right apical expansion tests; Mermaid (Right Sidelying Right Apical Expansion with Left Arm Reach and Left Adductor); seated resisted alternating tricep pull-downs; seated right scapular pull-back with right HG - if some tests become + again after upright alternating, revisit.

**Hruska Classification of Scapular Resting Position & Testing** - appendix item on Day 2 agenda; use when scapular-thoracic instability is the complaint after thorax neutrality attempts.

---

## 4. Inhibit vs facilitate (how I&I uses intro tables)

Same composite facilitate/inhibit tables as intros. I&I-specific emphasis:
- After repositioning, **facilitate opposition muscles of Left AIC / Right BC**  
- Chronic: build **Right AIC / Left BC** tri-planar capacity  
- HG IR: facilitate **right subscapularis**, **not** right latissimus or pec major (explicit treatment guideline language)  
- Scapular-thoracic: Right low trap/tricep → Left low trap/serratus → Right serratus → Right subscapularis (same neuromotor order as Postural Respiration; I&I applies it when instability/impingement persist)

---

## 5. Repositioning / treatment hierarchies (selected)

### General order philosophy
1. Reposition (intro non-manual/manual as needed)  
2. Ensure PRI tests support neutrality  
3. Address joint IR and opposition strength  
4. Progress plane-by-plane; do not skip firing-sequence steps  
5. Integrate upright reciprocal alternating activity only when tests stay negative  

### Snapping hip hierarchy (manual)
1. Reposition  
2. Ipsilateral Adduction and Abduction Lift scores of 3 or better with contralateral obturator foramen / ischium sense; consider sidelying supported left medial and posterior expansion with ipsilateral hip flexor inhibition; sidelying lateral thoracic expansion with balloon / intercostal inhibition to allow glute med shortening  
3. For left frontal/transverse FA instability maximize left calcaneal eversion; for right, right calcaneal eversion (Calcaneal Eversion Programs)  
4. Stabilize adductor activity in frontal plane - Standing Left AF IR with contralateral FA adduction; Standing Resisted Adductor Pull In; with left IO/TA; etc.  
5. Left stance upright integration / right stance upright integration activities  

### Knee / medial tibial / Left FA IR cluster hierarchy themes
Achieve bilateral lift tests ≥3; maximize Right AF ER strength/control; balance hamstrings (left medial hamstring appendix); Standing Supported Left AF IR with Right FA Abduction (Integration).

### Ilio-sacral instability
Restore iliacus / glute med-min / biceps femoris / adductor brevis / pectineus positional efficiency; do not chase sacral symptoms without swing-phase ilium force closure.

### Right BC PRI treatment guidelines (I&I application)
- Right apical expansion family (including Mermaid variant with left arm reach + left adductor)  
- Seated resisted alternating tricep pull-downs  
- Seated right scapular pull-back with right HG  
- If tests return + after upright alternating → regress  

### Right BC position progression (overview page - mirrors Postural)
Right low trap & right tricep → Left low trap & left serratus → Right serratus → Right subscapularis, with supine/sidelying/seated/standing/all-four/prone position ladders.

### Right subscapularis program themes
Supine resisted right HG IR; supine resisted right tricep extension with right HG IR; sidelying trunk lift variants; seated resisted pull-downs with right HG IR and left HG ER. Explicit rule: **facilitate right HG IR with right subscapularis, not lat or pec major.**

### Example upright integration titles appearing in I&I
- Standing Resisted Right Diagonal Flexion  
- Standing Supported Left AF IR with Left IO/TA and Resisted Right Posterior Glute Med  
- Left Stance in Left AF IR from Left AIC pattern (right arm reach, head slightly right, inhale nose / exhale reach)  
- Right medial hamstring program (left sidelying supported right glute max with right hip extension and right FA IR; TFL inhibition variants; standing wall-supported Left AF IR with knee flexion and right trunk rotation; prone right hip extension with FA IR/ER)

---

## 6. What NOT to do / common errors

- Do **not** treat positional impingement as primary bony "spurs first" without clearing Left AIC/Right BC patterning.  
- Do **not** strengthen into the patterned IR with lat-dominated HG IR - that feeds superior posterior HG impingement mechanics.  
- Do **not** skip progression steps or allow incorrect firing sequences (listed pitfalls).  
- Do **not** call multidirectional instability "core weakness" without counting **how many PRI tests are negative across planes**.  
- Do **not** jump to chronic Right AIC/Left BC max strength before acute/recurrent repositioning + IR restoration.  
- Do **not** ignore foot/calcaneal frontal-plane pieces when FA frontal-plane instability keeps returning.  
- Do **not** use I&I as a first course - intros first (Myokinematic / Pelvis / Postural).  

---

## 7. How courses link

| Stage | Course |
|---|---|
| Unlock AF/FA & Left AIC LE tests | [Myokinematic Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-myokinematic-restoration) |
| Inlet/outlet & pelvic diaphragm hold | [Pelvis Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-pelvis-restoration) |
| ZOA / Right BC / PEC thorax | [Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) |
| When neutrality exists intermittently but joints impinge or go multi-directionally unstable; scapular-thoracic & HG IR details; calcaneal/knee/FA/IS tables | **This course** |

Postural Respiration treatment guidelines explicitly route "all BC tests − but insufficient right scapular-thoracic function" toward BC manuals (Infraclavicular Pump, Sibson, Intercostal) and right serratus - that is the doorway into I&I thinking for the upper quarter.

---

## 8. Achieve programming translation

- Overhead/swim athletes with lat-dominant IR and scapular winging after breathing work → subscapularis + serratus + low trap order; inhibit lat.  
- Recurrent groin/hip "impingement" language from athletes → screen ADT/FA IR/AF IR and pattern before loading deep flexion IR under load.  
- Medial knee / footwear complaints with Left AIC → lift-test gates + Left AF IR integration; don't only strengthen VMO.  
- Keep I&I as the "why the joint keeps yelling after intros" reference, not the first warm-up picker - start with [PRI breathing exercise selection](sand-workflow:pri-breathing-exercise-selection) then the matching intro skill.

Open the full OCR reference for complete pathology tables, calcaneal programs, and appendix exercise numbers.

# PRI Myokinematic Restoration (course skill)

**Source (full text):** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-myokinematic-restoration.txt`  
*(OCR from scanned PDF - cross-check coaching cues against clean reprints in Pelvis Restoration appendix when wording is noisy.)*  
**Manual:** *Myokinematic Restoration - An Integrated Approach to Treatment of Patterned Lumbo-Pelvic-Femoral Pathomechanics* (PRI; revision noted Feb 2017 in OCR'd copy).  
**Course family:** Introductory course with Pelvis Restoration and Postural Respiration.

---

## 1. Core theory / asymmetry model (this course)

Myokinematic Restoration owns **acetabulum-on-femur (AF) and femur-on-acetabulum (FA)** pathomechanics of the Left AIC pattern - how the pelvis orients the hip socket and how the femur orients in that socket across stance/swing.

### Stance / pattern definitions (manual)
- **Left stance in Left AF IR = Right AIC pattern** (desired alternating opposite)  
- **Right stance in Right AF IR = Left AIC pattern** (typical compensatory default)  
- **Right stance in Left AF ER = Left AIC pattern** (same family)

**Desirable "real estate" for repositioning:** maximize **Left AF IR & Right AF ER** and motor control in that orientation. Left AF ER / Right AF IR is the patterned Left AIC state to leave.

### Why Left AIC dominates lumbo-pelvic-femoral findings
Same systemic asymmetry as other intros (right hemi-diaphragm + liver, right stance bias). Left pelvis anterior/forward → femur biomechanically oriented; psoas fails as femoral ER; VL and biceps femoris become antagonistic stabilizers (shared AIC description across manuals). Symptoms can present at knee, hip, groin, SI, back, shoulder blade, neck, face/TMJ with inability to fully adduct/extend/flex one or both sides and limited trunk rotation.

### Positional influences (themes from manual sections)
Patients stuck in **right AF IR + left AF ER** show characteristic length/strength imbalances:
- Posterior glute med (ER): long/weak secondary to adduction + IR  
- Anterior glute med (IR): long secondary to adduction but can be short/strong positionally  
- Hamstrings: proximal attachment more forward/elevated secondary to anterior innominate rotation → SLR looks "tight" while group is long, hypotonic, cortically suppressed  
- Right adductors / FA IRs overactive; femoral head can impinge anterior-medial acetabular cotyloid rim on FA ER secondary to right AF IR osseous position  

### Soft tissue / capsule after repositioning
If capsular/soft-tissue issues remain after pelvic repositioning (over-compensatory activity):
- At 90° flexion, IR can be checked by superior ischiofemoral ligament and/or inferior capsule  
- At 90° flexion, ER can be checked by iliofemoral ligament and/or superior capsule  
Manual pairs stretches + AF/FA muscle strategies (IC adductor approximation, AF ER glute max, anterior/posterior glute med, obturator foramen control) by which rotation is limited left vs right.

---

## 2. Patterns to recognize

### Non-patho compensatory Left AIC (Myokinematic test results table)
| PRI test | Typical Left AIC result |
|---|---|
| Adduction Drop Test | + Left (unable to adduct left) |
| Extension Drop Test | often related findings; + L EDT with + L ADT relationships discussed |
| Straight Leg Raise | ↓ Left SLR |
| Trunk Rotation | Limited right trunk rotation (legs/rotation toward left limited in the patterned sense described) |
| FA ROM | ↓ Left FA IR ROM; ↓ Right FA ER ROM (vs opposite) |
| Hruska Adduction Lift | Level findings (often limited early levels on patterned side) |
| Hruska Abduction Lift | Level findings (e.g. Level 2 right noted in table OCR) |

### Functional relationships (manual shorthand)
- + L ADT with + L EDT relationships; − L EDT ↔ iliofemoral/pubofemoral laxity themes  
- Limited R trunk rotation vs non-limited (right iliolumbar laxity note)  
- ↓ L SLR = long, neuromuscularly weak, hypotonic, overly stretched "inactive" hamstring group  
- ↓ L FA IR ROM secondary to left AF ER osseous position  
- ↓ R FA ER ROM secondary to overactive right adductors/FA IRs + anterior-medial rim impingement in right AF IR  
- + R ADT with + L ADT → think **PEC** (hand off toward Pelvis / Postural Respiration)  
- L AF IR = R AF ER ↔ Right AIC (desired); R AF IR = L AF ER ↔ Left AIC (patterned)

### Femoral Acetabular ROM (seated) interpretation
Seated FA IR/ER with hips/knees ~90° (vs prone) to keep ligamentous site more resting. In non-pathologic compensatory Left AIC:
- ↓ L FA IR may reflect abducted left femur in L AF ER when legs face examiner → femur hits posterior-inferior acetabular rim on FA IR  
- ↓ R FA ER may reflect adducted right femur in R AF IR → femur "impinges" anterior-superior-medial acetabular rim on FA ER  

**After successful repositioning without osseous/capsular block:** expect ↑ L FA IR and ↑ R FA ER toward normal vs pre-repositioning. If still restricted → soft-tissue pathology pathway (not just "more stretching blindly").

### FA neuromuscular control
Seated FA IR/ER strength; note **which muscle the patient feels on FA IR strength** (glute med vs TFL). TFL dominance = need repositioning / different facilitator strategy (manual testing note).

---

## 3. Assessment / special tests (this course)

### Core battery (evaluation form + test chapters)
1. **Adduction Drop Test (ADT)** - position / Left AIC flag  
2. **Extension Drop Test (EDT)** - hip ligamentous laxity / extension pathomechanics  
3. **Trunk Rotation**  
4. **Straight Leg Raise (SLR)**  
5. **FA IR / FA ER ROM** (goniometric, seated)  
6. **FA IR / FA ER strength** (+ which muscle felt on IR)  
7. **Hruska Adduction Lift Test**  
8. **Hruska Abduction Lift Test**  

Evaluation form also lists Pelvis / Postural / Cervical / Advanced Integration blocks - Myokinematic sits first for AF/FA.

### ADT
Same sidelying procedure as other courses. Positive usually left in Left AIC; bilateral → PEC family.

### Hruska Adduction Lift Test (named for leg on examiner's shoulder)
Example: patient left sidelying, right ankle on examiner's shoulder → **Right** Hruska Adduction Lift.  
Position: back rounded; uppermost LE on shoulder (neutral hip, extended knee); lower leg flexed; pelvis neutral (no forward/back upper-pelvis rotation).  
Mechanics (stop at failed step):  
1. Raise ankle of flexed lower leg to upper knee  
2. Raise flexed lower knee while keeping ankle to knee  
3. Raise lower hip maintaining above  
Grading themes: early failure ↔ FA ER weakness or AF stability failure of active extremity; higher levels demand IC adductor / obturator / pelvic diaphragm / oblique integration (OCR levels 1-5).

### Hruska Abduction Lift Test
Named for leg on wall (e.g. left sidelying, right foot on wall → Right test). Used as myokinematic measurement of muscle position, strength, timing.  
Steps (stop at failure): press bottom toes to wall → press bottom hip into surface (lower abs/adductors) → turn/raise bottom knee inward (IC adductor + anterior glute med) without top hip moving back → turn top heel up / toes down without dropping bottom knee → raise top leg off wall with trunk/hips stabilized.  
Also used in **Pelvis Restoration** algorithms as a progression gate (e.g. 3/5 before upright frontal-plane control).

---

## 4. Inhibit vs facilitate (Myokinematic composite)

### General AIC (Myokinematic column)
**Facilitate:** hamstrings, ischiocondylar adductor, gluteus maximus, anterior glute med/min, posterior glute med/min, IO/TA  
**Inhibit:** TFL, adductor magnus, psoas major, piriformis, vastus lateralis  

### As related to Left AIC / Right BC / Right TMCC
**Facilitate:** L AF hamstrings, L AF IC adductor, R AF glute max, L FA anterior glute med/min, R FA posterior glute med/min, L IO/TA  
**Inhibit:** L TFL, R FA adductor magnus, L psoas major, L FA piriformis, R AF piriformis, R vastus lateralis  

Muscles that pull **femur into acetabulum** vs **acetabulum onto femur** are distinguished (glute max vs glute med/min themes) - AF IR work is not "more clamshells."

---

## 5. Repositioning logic and exercise progressions

### Course-selection gate (from Pelvis Identification page - critical)
After Left AIC repositioning attempt:
- **− L ADT / − L PADT → stay in Myokinematic Restoration Program**  
- **− L ADT / + L PADT → Pelvis Restoration Program**  

Bilateral:
- **− B ADT / − B PADT → Myokinematic + Postural Respiration**  
- **− B ADT / + B PADT → Pelvis Restoration**  

### Left AIC repositioning menu (clean cues from Pelvis appendix reprint of Myokinematic techniques)

**1. 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge**  
Feet on wall, hips/knees 90°. Exhale into pelvic tilt (tailbone slightly off; low back flat). Dig heels (not flat feet). Maintain tilt on left; straighten right; slowly on/off wall with breath - feel left posterior thigh. 3×10.

**2. Right Sidelying Respiratory Left Adductor Pull Back**  
Right sidelying, feet on wall, hips/knees 90°, ankles/knees together, back rounded. Bolster between feet; towel between knees; left knee lower than left hip/ankle. Push right foot into wall. Inhale - pull left leg back; exhale - squeeze left knee into towel 3s. Repeat 4-5 breaths, pulling further each inhale. ×5 sequences.

**3. Left Sidelying Right Glute Max**  
Left sidelying, feet on wall, hips/knees 90°, back rounded. Towel under ankles and left abs. Press left hip down (right hip toward wall) - feel left abs. Shift right hip forward to slight stretch left outer hip. Turn right knee out using wall as fulcrum without right hip moving back - feel right outer hip. 4-5 breaths. ×5.

### Hierarchy themes (agenda: Left AIC Myokinematic Hierarchy; Femoroacetabular / AF IR programs)
Progress from repositioning → FA/AF ROM & strength restoration → Hruska lift level improvements → upright Left AF IR / Right AF ER integration (standing wall-supported left knee flexion with resisted right glute max; all-four right glute max; standing resisted patterns; lateral walking integration; right adductor magnus inhibition in hooklying; left posterior capsule inhibition standing; QL/psoas inhibition pairs).

**Right piriformis syndrome considerations** (manual section): Right Sidelying Respiratory Resisted Left Adductor Pull Back; sidelying obturator/reciprocal techniques; standing wall-supported ischial femoral ligamentous stretch; seated supported Left AF IR with right iliacus and right FA ER; retro stairs with resisted glute max - as listed on that considerations page.

### Inhibition examples (appendix titles)
- Supine Hooklying Adductor Magnus Inhibition (right) - pelvic tilt + allow right knee to bolster; breathing holds  
- Left Posterior Capsule Inhibition - standing variants  
- Right QL and Left Psoas Inhibition - supine banded variants  

---

## 6. What NOT to do / common errors

- Do **not** stretch "tight hamstrings" as the primary fix when ↓ SLR reflects anterior innominate / long inhibited hamstrings.  
- Do **not** strengthen TFL-dominant FA IR - note which muscle is felt; reposition and facilitate glute med/IC adductor pathways.  
- Do **not** chase FA ER on the right with brute force while still in Right AF IR osseous position (rim impingement risk).  
- Do **not** keep someone in Myokinematic-only work when **PADT stays +** after − ADT - that is Pelvis Restoration.  
- Do **not** skip hemibridge / adductor pull-back / right glute max repositioning before advanced Hruska lift upright integration.  
- Do **not** interpret bilateral + ADT as "two unilateral Left AIC programs" only - PEC path.  
- Hruska lift compensations (flexing contralateral FA, pressing too hard into examiner's shoulder, lumbar extension instead of FA extension) invalidate the grade - coach the test, don't inflate the score.

---

## 7. How courses link

| Need | Open |
|---|---|
| AF/FA Left AIC, ADT/EDT/SLR/Hruska lifts, AF IR real estate | **This skill** |
| Inlet/outlet, PADT/PART, Patho PEC, pelvic diaphragm | [Pelvis Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-pelvis-restoration) |
| ZOA, Right BC, PEC thorax, apical expansion, serratus/low trap | [Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) |
| Positional impingement / multi-directional instability after patterning | [Impingement & Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) |

Myokinematic is the AF/FA foundation. Pelvis asks whether the pelvic diaphragm/inlet-outlet can hold what Myokinematic unlocks. Postural asks whether the thorax/ZOA can breathe in that pelvis. I&I asks what happens when neutrality is intermittent and joints start impinging or going multidirectionally unstable.

---

## 8. Achieve programming translation

- Warm-up Left AIC: hemibridge → adductor pull-back → right glute max sidelying as indicated by ADT/SLR/FA ROM.  
- Retro stairs / standing Left AF IR wall drills when frontal-plane shift is the limiter.  
- Pair right-stance-biased athletes with left AF IR reference centers (left heel, left abs, left ischial seat, right arch).  
- If PADT + after ADT clears → switch programming reference to Pelvis skill.  
- OCR reference path is searchable for appendix exercise numbers when you need the exact non-manual title.

Open the full reference text for complete hierarchy pages, FA soft-tissue tables, and evaluation form fields.

# PRI Primary Non-Manual Techniques Workshop

**Sources (synthesized into one skill):**
- Typed notes (clean cues): `.../memory/reference/pri-nm-techniques-workshop-typed-notes.txt` - Feb 2023 workshop notes  
- Complete manual (structure/hierarchies): `.../memory/reference/pri-primary-nm-techniques-workshop-manual.txt` - *PRImary Non-Manual Techniques Workshop* complete manual Feb 2023 (© 2018-2023 PRI)

**Extraction quality:** Both PDFs yielded searchable text via `pdftotext` (no OCR required). Manual is image-heavy for technique photos (positional outline pages are mostly figure plates); use typed notes for coaching cues and manual for program organization / reference-center theory.

Prefer **non-manual** techniques in Achieve. This skill teaches when-to-use families, cueing, reference/referent logic, and neuro-motor order - not a full reprint of 300+ CD techniques.

Cross-links: [PRI Myokinematic Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-myokinematic-restoration) · [PRI Pelvis Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-pelvis-restoration) · [PRI Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) · [PRI Right BC Treatment Guidelines](sand-workflow:pri-right-bc-treatment-guidelines) · [PRI breathing exercise selection](sand-workflow:pri-breathing-exercise-selection) · [PRI Impingement and Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability)

---

## 1. How PRI Non-Manual programs are organized

Introductory courses each have Non-Manual CDs organized by **muscle, inhibition, and integration**, ordered by how you would isolate → inhibit → integrate. Integration program: 300+ techniques across nine positions; Integration symbol = thorax-pelvis via abdominals (**inhibit a pattern / facilitate a position** - not "strengthen abs").

**Reference centers (Integration):** left abdominals, left ischial seat, left heel, right arch.

### Terminology in titles
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Respiratory | Phase of respiration that expands L posterior mediastinum, L posterior outlet, or L posterior hip capsule |
| Reciprocal | Full available ROM both directions |
| Alternating | One side then the other (e.g. 3 breaths L then 3 R) |
| Supported | Proprioceptive surface (wall, floor foot, pillow, table) |
| Resisted | Band |
| Weighted | Free weight |

### Hard progression rules
- Neuro-motor position order follows Integration demand (exceptions: R Glute Max differs Myo vs Pelvis; Inhibition programs; R Low Trap/Tricep order on Postural CD).  
- **Bilateral inhibition always precedes unilateral.**  
- If a technique "looks in the wrong muscle folder," assume intentional facilitation via inhibitory muscle/position/process - don't reshuffle by bodybuilding logic.  
- Example: 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge **always** precedes 90-90 Hip Lift with Balloon.

### Why BC muscle order is R LT/Tricep → L LT/Serratus → R Serratus → R Subscap
Typical L AIC + R BC: pelvis/spine/diaphragm oriented right; thorax rotates back left above diaphragm for frontal balance and R reach. Right-handedness promotes that left upper rotation and disadvantages R low trap / triceps / serratus.

1. **R low trap + tricep** - retract/posterior-tilt scapula; stabilize spine with L abs; elbow extension; thoracic flexion; lat down.  
2. **L low trap + L serratus** - reorient upper thorax; stabilize upper quadrants during R reach.  
3. **R serratus** - stabilize R scapula for R reach **without** needing left upper trunk rotation.  
4. **R subscap** - HG IR independent of overactive lat (after neutrality).

Later positions in each muscle set demand **more isolation with more substitution inhibition**.

---

## 2. Position decision-making (advantages)

| Position | Best for |
|---|---|
| Supine | Bilateral sensory comparison; ANS outcomes (SLR); cranial-pelvis sagittal tilt; early facilitation |
| Sidelying | Best **non-dominant unilateral compensatory inhibition** |
| All Four | Flexed appendage co-activation during thoraco-abdominal flexion; best respiratory position |
| Short Seated | Best passive reposition |
| Long Seated | Best desirable position to strive for and maintain |
| Seated | Thoracic-pelvis rotation without thoracic-cervical hyperactivity |
| Standing | Re-biasing alternating lateralized cortical / centering sense |
| Prone | Inhibit L TFL via L FA IR |
| Kneeling | L glute med isolation with hamstrings shortened |

---

## 3. Course positional outlines (families to open)

### Myokinematic Restoration (examples of muscle folders)
Left Hamstring → Left IC Adductor → Right Glute Max → Left Glute Med → Left Hip Flexor Inhibition → Left TFL Inhibition → … (position ladders: supine → sidelying → long seated → seated → standing → all four → prone as listed per muscle).

### Pelvis Restoration
Right Rectus Femoris/Sartorius, Left Obturator/Iliococcygeus, Left Iliacus, Right Glute Max (different order than Myo), inlet/outlet inhibition folders (L anterior inlet, R anterior outlet, R posterior inlet, L posterior outlet), etc.

### Postural Respiration
Right Lower Trap & Right Tricep → Left Lower Trap & Left Serratus → Right Serratus → Right Subscapularis; plus Paravertebral / Pectoral / Lat / Intercostal / Anterior Neck inhibition families.

Open the matching course skill for test gates (ADT/PADT, apical, etc.) before picking a folder.

---

## 4. Workshop technique cards (from typed notes - Achieve-usable)

Each card: **Reference / Referent(s)** → inhibit → who it's for → coaching notes.

### Right Sidelying Left Adductor Pull Back with Knee to Knee
- **Ref:** L post calcaneus/heel (low). **Referents:** L IO/TA (high), R med long arch (low).  
- **Inhibit:** R thoracic diaphragm (by empowering left); L post outlet / L ant inlet / R post inlet / R ant outlet; L posterior ground with R forward movement; L rearfoot with L abs + R forefoot (late double stance → left shift).  
- **For:** difficulty rotating upper trunk R while lower trunk left; need left "load" to free R arm/chest (static/overtight right).  
- **Cues:** Push L hand into floor → R trunk rotation with L AF IR (L IO/TA). Sense leftward retro. Lower upper body to floor before going vertical. Also inhibits L short FA ERs, R short AF IRs, R short back rotators (R QL, R IO/TA).

### Left Sidelying Foot Toward Ceiling with Resisted Right Glute Max and Right Apical Expansion
- **Ref:** L ischial seat (mod), R med long arch (low). **Referents:** R lat post upper chest (R LT/triceps), L ant AF capsule (L adductor), L IO/TA, R post hip (R glute max).  
- **Inhibit:** Overuse R IO/TA/EO + R rectus; R BC; R hip flexor (psoas+TFL); TF ERs; R intercostals.  
- **For:** sense of left / shift left; R thoracic curve; R mouse/computer; R shoulder impingement; interscap pain / flat backs; limited R cervical lateral flexion; post R subclavius release.  
- **Cues:** L HG ER (teres minor/infraspinatus) helps posterior mediastinal expansion and forces R apical up; cross-ref anterior rib abs with posterior scapular stabilizers + SA.

### Stair Short Seated Balloon
- **Ref:** L ischial seat. **Referents:** L IO/TA, L post calcaneal tuberosity, R med long arch, L post mediastinum, R lat post upper chest.  
- **Inhibit:** R hemilateral foot/ischial/ZOA "grounding"; lat / longissimus / interscap; quads.  
- **For:** unsteady left foot / can't pause without leaning back-right; wide BOS gait; can't squat from short quads/hip flexors.  
- **Cues:** Best position to establish posterior mediastinums **and** upper lateral chest expansion on inhale **and** exhale; prep for retro / cranio activity.

### Long Seated Press Down
- **Ref:** R lat post upper chest (R LT/tricep) R>L; L post heel L>R. **Referent:** L IO/TA L>R.  
- **Inhibit:** Hip and neck flexors via hamstring-tricep cross-reference.  
- **For:** protracted shoulders + deep lumbar curve; periscapular weakness; bicipital tendinitis; sitters who overwork rectus + anterior chest/neck.  
- **Cues:** Awareness of 90° SLR with neutral thoracic orientation; balance mid/lower trap, SA, rhomboids, subscap with tricep; enhances subscap/SA with abs + dorsiflexion.

### Seated Supported Respiratory Left AF IR/FA IR with Intercostal Pulley Inhibition
- **Ref:** L ischial tuberosity. **Referents:** R LT/tricep, L ant AF capsule (adductor), L IO/TA, R med long arch.  
- **Inhibit:** R IO/TA; R upper trap; R scalenes/BC; R intercostals; L TFL; patterned inlet/outlet set; R posterior mediastinum; L levator.  
- **For:** poor R overhead reach sitting/standing; can't reach up/out while turning upper body same side.  
- **Cues:** Sense L adductors + L glute med/min during L posterior mediastinum + R apical expansion; pelvic/hip anchor for contralateral release.

### 90-90 Supported Wall Leg Lift with Alternating Resisted Arm Reach
- **A ref:** L heel; referents R glute max, L IO/TA, L post mediastinum.  
- **B ref:** R heel; referents L glute max, R LT/tricep, L post mediastinum.  
- **Inhibit:** A = L AIC/R BC; B = L low-back extension + L LT/triceps.  
- **For:** dissociation issues; poor ground friction sense + scapula-on-thorax friction; flat back / flat affect / rigid.  
- **Cues:** Alternating secures LE for ipsilateral lower torso rotation + contralateral upper torso rotation **without** cervical help; intro to retro; both pictures get L posterior mediastinum (A via L SA + L hammies; B via R SA + left leg lift).

### Right Sidelying Left Anterior Glute Med with TFL Inhibition
- **Ref:** L ischial tuberosity. **Referents:** L IO/TA, R glute max.  
- **Inhibit:** L TFL; R hip adductors; L rectus femoris.  
- **For:** poor L single-leg strength (step overs/throughs); flat L feet / don't know how to pronate.  
- **Mods:** Ball between knees → more ant glute med/min; bolster under R ankle → more R FA ER vs abd; light weight on L ankle → more L glute demand.

### Left Sidelying Supported Trunk Lift
- **Ref:** L IO/TA, L heel. **Referent:** R LT/triceps.  
- **Inhibit:** R calcaneus; R ischial seat; L canines / R molars; L post hip; L LT/triceps (+ R bicep/pec); R ant AF capsule; R IO/TA.  
- **For:** vestibular leftward figure-8 difficulty; Superior T4; L hemidiaphragm weakness/SOB; clenchers; post MMOO/MOOO orthotic.  
- **Cues:** Pillow under pelvis aligns pelvis-cranial bowls; wall anchors feet for torso-pelvis-cranium axis.

### Seated Resisted Reciprocal Pull Downs
- Keep upper trunk turned right. A emphasize inhale; B emphasize exhale.  
- **Inhibit:** A = L upper trap / L apical / R BC; B = R upper trap / R abs / L anterior BC.  
- **For:** retrain alternating trunk with L pelvis/hip security; cervicalgia / temporal-frontal HA.  
- Lower chair → more heel / ischial / ST / OA extension R>L demand.

### Single Leg Stance with Contralateral Glute Max
- Block under foot = hemi vestibular-postural demand; pole in R hand for balance / compression bias.  
- **Inhibit:** A = back extensors esp R QL/paravertebrals; B = L pec minor.  
- **For:** A LBP / weak quads / overused L VL; B L AIC reposition / weak L FA IRs in hip extension.

### Standing Supported Bilateral IO/TA
- **Inhibit:** glossopharyngeal, tongue, shoulder elevators, upper traps, lats, plantarflexors.  
- **For:** forward head; sleep apnea; laryngeal tension; swallowing issues.  
- **Cues:** Retro BOS sense; Functional Squat Test ≥3 allows abs to rotate torso; arms overhead with eccentric hammies/adductors; intro R then L arm reach.

### Standing Left Knee Flexion with Right AIC Progression
- **Inhibit:** latero-spatial single-leg transfer sense; hip flexors; R quads.  
- **For:** SLR >90° bilaterally (abs as rotators, hammies stabilize); LBP/SI; limited L shoulder flexion (pulls L thorax under L scapula); R tennis elbow from over-supination; R quad overuse.  
- Ground sense lifts on **left** secondary to R UE extension position.

### Standing Supported Left Glute Push
- Valsalva-like between exhale and inhale without balloon/nose pinch; lift R LE → R psoas + R FA ER to keep mass left.  
- **Inhibit:** anterior neck / scalenes / accessory respirators.  
- **For:** autonomic dysfunction / dysautonomia (see PRI Breathing Mechanics in COVID Times week 3 handout referenced in notes).

### Modified Two Point Gait with Left AF IR
- Poles slow pelvis timing vs scapular alternation; R pole lever with R triceps → R LT + pelvic floor for L AF IR cognition.  
- **Inhibit:** ipsilateral UE-LE ambulatory pattern (R UE with R LE / L with L).  
- **For:** ataxia; scissor gait.

### Standing Right Knee Flexion with Resisted Left Hamstring and Right Trunk Rotation
- **Inhibit:** L hip flexors; R SCM; R BC (pecs); R hip adductors; L trunk rotation / R IO/TA.  
- **For:** R PF pain / quad tendinitis; R LE centering during L hip adduction; bilateral lat / back-over-extension users.  
- Mimics resisted decline retro walk (L abs; R floor back / R foot forward during L hip extension).

---

## 5. When to open which family (coach decision map)

| Goal / finding | Start family |
|---|---|
| Need ZOA / L AIC inhibition / balloon | 90-90 family, Stair Short Seated Balloon, Wall Supported Squat Balloon |
| Need L AF IR + R freedom | R Sidelying L Adductor Pull Back; Seated Respiratory L AF IR + intercostal pulley |
| Need R apical + shift left | L Sidelying Foot Toward Ceiling + R glute max / R apical |
| Need PEC / paraspinal down | Stair Short Seated Balloon; Standing Supported Bilateral IO/TA; Paraspinal inhibition folder; Functional Squat families |
| BC tests − → R LT/tricep | Long Seated Press Down; Seated/Standing Alternating Tricep Pulldowns; Sidelying Trunk Lift R |
| Need L serratus stabilize | 90-90 Wall Leg Lift Alternating Reach; Standing Serratus Squat; All Four Belly Lift Reach |
| Need true R HG IR | R Subscap folder **after** neutrality (not lat IR) |
| Single-leg / gait | Single Leg Stance Contralateral Glute; Modified Two-Point Gait L AF IR; Standing R Knee Flexion + L hammie |

Always re-test course screens after a technique block.

---

## 6. What NOT to do

- Cherry-pick "cool" late positions (prone/standing isolations) before early ones work.  
- Unilateral inhibition before bilateral.  
- Cue techniques as ab hypertrophy or generic mobility.  
- Ignore reference/referent sensing - without tactile co-reference the neuro outcome weakens.  
- Skip course test gates and jump folders by symptom name alone ("shoulder" → random serratus).

---

## 7. Achieve programming translation

- Warm-up: 1-2 repositioning techniques from the map (often 90-90 balloon or stair short seated balloon + one sidelying).  
- Tertiary: match folder to remaining test (R LT/tricep vs L serratus vs inhibition).  
- Write **reference sense** in athlete cues ("left heel + left abs," "right arch," "left sit bone").  
- Swimmers: bias Stair Short Seated Balloon / Wall Reach / All Four Belly Lift Reach / R apical sidelying + later R subscap only after BC neutrality language.  
- Keep clinician manuals (Superior T4, Subclavius, Infraclavicular) out of gym improvisation - see Right BC guidelines skill.

Open course skills for theory depth; open this skill for technique selection and cueing.

# PRI Pelvis Restoration (course skill)

**Source (full text):** `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/pri-pelvis-restoration.txt`  
**Manual:** *Pelvis Restoration - An Integrated Approach to Treatment of Patterned Pubo-Sacral Pathomechanics* (PRI, © 2010-2024).  
**Course family:** Introductory course alongside Myokinematic Restoration and Postural Respiration.

Expert reference for Achieve programming and intelligent discussion. Not a license to diagnose or perform manual pelvic techniques.

---

## 1. Core theory / asymmetry model (this course)

Pelvis Restoration reframes the Left AIC / PEC problem in **pelvic inlet and outlet** language and ties the **pelvic diaphragm** to the respiratory diaphragm (reciprocal and alternating goals).

### Left AIC pelvic position summary (manual)
- **LEFT:** Inlet IP ER = IS IR = Outlet IsP IR = AF ER  
- **RIGHT:** Inlet IP IR = IS ER = Outlet IsP ER = AF IR  

(Translation for coaches: left hemi-pelvis is stuck in the pattern that blocks left AF IR / left frontal-plane shift; right side is the stance-biased opposite.)

### Neuro-muscular facilitation goals - to inhibit a Left AIC (inlet/outlet map)

**Pelvic Inlet**
| Side | Action | Key muscles (manual colors/labels) |
|---|---|---|
| Left | IP IR anterior inlet (Ext/Add/IR) | IO/TA |
| Right | IP ER anterior inlet (Flex/Abd/ER) | Rectus femoris, sartorius |
| Left | IS ER posterior inlet | Iliacus, gluteus medius |
| Right | IS IR posterior inlet | Gluteus maximus (superior fibers) |

**Pelvic Outlet**
| Side | Action | Key muscles |
|---|---|---|
| Left | IsP ER anterior outlet (Flex/Abd/ER) | Hamstring, IC adductor, obturator, iliococcygeus |
| Right | SI IR posterior outlet | Gluteus maximus (inferior fibers), piriformis, coccygeus |

### PEC pattern summary
- **Pelvic inlet:** Bilateral IP ER / IS IR - anterior sacrum flexed  
- **Pelvic outlet:** Bilateral IsP IR - posterior sacrum extended; coccyx flexed  
- Pelvic diaphragm **positionally descended, hypertonic, inflexible**  
Manual axiom: **"Behind every PEC is a Left AIC pattern."**

### Patho PEC position summary
Same bilateral inlet/outlet directional description as PEC, but pelvic diaphragm is **descended, bulged, and high resting tone** - a more pathologic pelvic-floor / outlet presentation. Patho-specific tests are bolded in the test matrix (below).

### Respiratory influence themes (course sections)
- Left AIC: hemi-diaphragm / hemi-pelvis coupling; left posterior outlet mediastinum expansion matters  
- PEC: bilateral anterior rib flare/ER; bilateral posterior mediastinum restriction  
- Patho PEC: same extension bias with greater pelvic diaphragm dysfunction  

Apical Expansion Test and Posterior Outlet Mediastinum Expansion Test appear in algorithms as respiratory companions to pelvis tests.

---

## 2. Patterns to recognize

### Left AIC (pelvis course)
+ Left ADT; often + Left PADT; + Right PART; Standing Reach > 0"; Functional Squat < 3/5; Hruska Abduction Lift < 3/5. Person cannot shift into left AF IR / control left outlet abduction and right outlet adduction in gait terms.

### PEC
+ Bilateral ADT; + Bilateral PADT; Standing Reach > 0"; PART − bilateral; Functional Squat < 3/5; Hruska Abd Lift < 3/5. Bilateral anterior inlet / posterior outlet bias; pelvic diaphragm descended/hypertonic.

### Patho PEC (* patho tests bolded in manual)
+ Bilateral ADT; **Standing Reach = 0"**; + Bilateral PADT; **PART + bilateral or unilateral**; **Functional Squat > 3/5**; Hruska Abd Lift < 3/5. Reach may look "better" while PART/squat pathology flags pelvic diaphragm / pathologic PEC.

### Ilio-sacral (IS) instability (Left AIC patients)
Separate hierarchy in the manual when IS instability overlays Left AIC - do not skip to aggressive alternating activity before inlet/outlet inhibition sequencing.

---

## 3. Assessment / special tests

### Battery (Pelvis Restoration Tests)
1. **Adduction Drop Test (ADT)** - Position  
2. **Standing Reach Test (SRT)** - Sagittal plane  
3. **Pelvic Ascension Drop Test (PADT)** - Frontal plane stance phase  
4. **Passive Abduction Raise Test (PART)** - Frontal plane swing phase  
5. **Functional Squat Test**  
6. **Hruska Abduction Lift Test** - also a Myokinematic measurement with pelvic interpretation  

Plus respiratory companions in algorithms: Left Posterior Outlet Mediastinum Expansion; Right Apical Expansion.

### ADT (detail)
Same sidelying procedure as other courses. Positive = femur will not adduct; reflective of osseous restriction from acetabular labral rim / related structures; usually left in Left AIC; bilateral in PEC/Patho PEC.

### Test matrices (when ADT is + left or bilateral)

**Left AIC**
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| ADT | + left |
| Standing Reach | > 0" |
| PADT | + left |
| PART | + right |
| Functional Squat | < 3/5 |
| Hruska Abd Lift | < 3/5 |

**PEC**
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| ADT | + bilateral |
| Standing Reach | > 0" |
| PADT | + bilateral |
| PART | − bilateral |
| Functional Squat | < 3/5 |
| Hruska Abd Lift | < 3/5 |

**Patho PEC**
| Test | Finding |
|---|---|
| ADT | + bilateral |
| *Standing Reach | 0" |
| PADT | + bilateral |
| *PART | + bilateral or unilateral |
| *Functional Squat | > 3/5 |
| Hruska Abd Lift | < 3/5 |

### Critical course-selection gates (PRI Identification page)
**Left AIC repositioning techniques** (candidates: 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge; Right Sidelying Respiratory Left Adductor Pull Back; Left Sidelying Right Glute Max) when + L ADT and + L PADT.

Decision:
- **− L ADT / + L PADT → Pelvis Restoration Program**  
- **− L ADT / − L PADT → Myokinematic Restoration Program**

**PEC / Patho PEC repositioning** (Standing Wall Supported Reach; 90-90 Hip Lift in Passive FA IR with Balloon; Modified All Four Belly Lift) when + B ADT and + B PADT.

Decision:
- **− B ADT / + B PADT → Pelvis Restoration Program**  
- **− B ADT / − B PADT → Myokinematic Restoration and Postural Respiration Program**

This is the clearest "which course owns this athlete today" rule in the three intros.

---

## 4. Inhibit vs facilitate (Pelvis composite)

From composite-of-courses tables (also printed in Postural manual):

**Pelvis Restoration - AIC chain (general)**  
- Facilitate **Pelvic Inlet:** proximal iliacus, sartorius, rectus femoris, IO/TA  
- Inhibit **Pelvic Inlet:** thoracic diaphragm, IO/EO, paravertebrals  
- Facilitate **Pelvic Outlet:** proximal obturator, iliococcygeus, puborectalis, pubococcygeus, glute max, piriformis, coccygeus  
- Inhibit **Pelvic Outlet:** adductor magnus, hamstrings  

**As related to Left AIC** (sided):  
Facilitate inlet L proximal iliacus, R sartorius, R rectus femoris, L IO/TA; outlet L proximal obturator, L iliococcygeus, L puborectalis/pubococcygeus, R glute max, R piriformis, R coccygeus.  
Inhibit inlet R thoracic hemi-diaphragm, R IO/EO, L paravertebrals; outlet R adductor magnus, R hamstrings, L piriformis, L coccygeus, L glute max.

**Goals language:** turn patterns from Left AIC "ON/OFF" maps toward **Right AIC alternating** (reciprocal and alternating pelvic and respiratory diaphragms). For PEC/Patho PEC, goals emphasize facilitation of abs with posterior pelvic tilt and proximal adductors into reciprocal inlet IP IR / outlet IsP ER bilaterally.

---

## 5. Repositioning logic, algorithms, hierarchies

### Left AIC Pattern - Pelvis Restoration Algorithm (test results cluster)
Typical positives: + L ADT, + SRT (can't touch toes), + L PADT, + R PART, <3/5 Functional Squat, <3/5 Hruska Abd Lift, + L Posterior Outlet Mediastinum Expansion, + R Apical Expansion.

**Repositioning menu**
1. 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge  
2. Right Sidelying Respiratory Left Adductor Pull Back  
3. Left Sidelying Right Glute Max  

**Branches**
- Repositions to **− L ADT, − L PADT, − R PART** → further assessment if still can't hold; may need other PRI courses  
- Remains **all tests +** or **− L ADT but + L PADT and/or + R PART** → **Pelvis Restoration Program** (maximize hemi 90-90 position)  
- Then when **− PADT** and **3/5 Hruska Abd Lift**: upright L single-leg frontal plane static/dynamic control (left outlet abduction) → upright R single-leg frontal plane (right outlet adduction) → sidelying frontal plane integration → seated left pelvic outlet ascension control → reciprocal alternating activity  

If unable to reposition pelvis: re-evaluate techniques or assessment tests from other PRI courses (manual).

### Left AIC Pelvis Restoration Hierarchy (when − L ADT and + L PADT and/or + R PART)

**Facilitation (Alternating) Program - sequenced:**
1. Turn **on right anterior pelvic inlet via IP ER** (rectus femoris + right sartorius)  
   - 90-90 Supported Left Hip Shift with Right Rectus Femoris and Sartorius  
   - Supine Hooklying Supported Right Rectus Femoris and Sartorius  
   - Supine Hemi Extension with Alternating Respiratory Rectus Femoris and Sartorius (R only)  
2. Turn **on left anterior pelvic outlet via IsP ER** (left puborectalis/pubococcygeus) with left inlet IP IR; turn on left iliococcygeus and left obturator via left adductors  
3. (continues in manual - inhibit right posterior inlet via IP ER to promote right inlet abduction; upright left single-leg frontal plane control; sidelying frontal plane integration; etc.)

**Inhibition (Alternating) Program - sequenced themes from manual:**
1. Inhibition sequencing paired with the above  
2. Inhibit right posterior inlet via IP ER to promote right inlet abduction  
3. Upright left single-leg frontal plane control (left outlet abduction via left iliacus and left …)  
4. Sidelying frontal plane integration (left inlet adduction and right inlet abduction with left …)  

Appendix inhibition families (non-manual titles to know):
- Left Anterior Inlet Inhibition (e.g. 90-90 Respiratory Left Hip …; 90-90 Supported Left Hip Shift with Right Rectus Femoris and Sartorius; Late Left AIC Stance with Right Arm Reach)  
- Right Anterior Outlet Inhibition (Supine Hooklying Adductor …)  
- Right Posterior Inlet Inhibition (All Four Right Glute Max …; Standing Supported Left Knee Flexion with Right Psoas …)  
- Left Posterior Outlet Inhibition (All Four Right Arm Reach …; Standing Supported Left Posterior Outlet Inhibition)  
- Bilateral Anterior Inlet + Bilateral Posterior Outlet Inhibition (Wall and Chair Supported …; Standing Wall Supported …; Squatting Bar Reverse …; Full Functional Squat …; squat & respiration notes)

### PEC Pattern - Pelvis Restoration Hierarchy
Gate: **− Bilateral ADT and (+ …)** per manual hierarchy page. Algorithm page pairs with PEC repositioning techniques and then PEC-specific facilitation/inhibition (abs + posterior pelvic tilt + proximal adductors; bilateral inlet/outlet goals).

### Pathologic PEC Pattern - Hierarchy / Algorithm
Gate: **− Bilateral ADT** with Patho test cluster. Emphasizes pelvic diaphragm / floor isolation considerations (appendix: treatment considerations for isolation of pelvic floor and transverse …). Higher caution; not a "just breathe harder" problem.

### Ilio-Sacral (IS) Instability Treatment Hierarchy for Left AIC patients
Separate ladder - address IS instability sequencing before assuming standard alternating gait integration will stick.

### Left AIC / PEC / Patho PEC repositioning technique lists (appendix)
**Left AIC:** 90-90 Supported Hip Lift with Hemibridge; Right Sidelying Respiratory Left Adductor Pull Back; Left Sidelying Right Glute Max (detailed cues in appendix - also cross-listed under Myokinematic appendix pages in this manual).  

**PEC / Patho PEC (bilateral anterior):** Standing Wall Supported Reach; 90-90 Hip Lift in Passive FA IR with Balloon; Modified All Four Belly Lift.

### Squat & respiration (appendix - Bilateral Anterior Inlet / Posterior Outlet section)
Manual includes dedicated squat ascend/descend respiratory coaching in the pelvis inhibition appendix (pair with Postural Respiration squat-breathing logic). In all variations, squat **ascend** is exhalation-biased to keep ribs down / extensors quiet.

---

## 6. What NOT to do / common errors

- Do **not** send someone to Myokinematic-only work when **− ADT / + PADT** - that is **Pelvis Restoration**.  
- Do **not** send someone to Pelvis-only work when **− ADT / − PADT** - that is **Myokinematic** (and for bilateral −/−, Myokinematic **+ Postural Respiration**).  
- Do **not** treat PEC as "two Left AICs" without bilateral test logic and bilateral inlet/outlet goals.  
- Do **not** miss Patho PEC: Standing Reach of **0"** with **+ PART** and **Functional Squat > 3/5** is not a win - it is a different bucket.  
- Do **not** skip repositioning into hemi 90-90 neutrality before upright single-leg frontal-plane drills.  
- Do **not** jump to reciprocal alternating activity before inlet/outlet facilitation-inhibition hierarchy and PADT resolution.  
- Do **not** ignore IS instability hierarchy in Left AIC patients who keep losing neutrality.  
- S&C should not improvise manual IP ER / IsP IR / pelvic floor techniques - keep non-manual menus.

---

## 7. How courses link

| Finding after repositioning attempt | Open |
|---|---|
| − L ADT / − L PADT | [Myokinematic Restoration](sand-workflow:pri-myokinematic-restoration) |
| − L ADT / + L PADT | **This course** |
| − B ADT / − B PADT | Myokinematic **and** [Postural Respiration](sand-workflow:pri-postural-respiration) |
| − B ADT / + B PADT | **This course** (PEC/Patho path) |
| Thorax/BC/apical/ZOA remain limited after pelvis neutrality | Postural Respiration |
| Scapular-thoracic / HG IR / impingement remain after BC tests − | [Impingement & Instability](sand-workflow:pri-impingement-instability) |

Pelvis Restoration sits between raw AF/FA myokinematics and thoraco-abdominal respiration: it owns **whether the pelvic diaphragm and inlet/outlet can alternate** so ZOA and AF IR can stick.

---

## 8. Achieve programming translation

- Choose breathing/repositioning from the **correct course gate** (PADT/PART vs ADT alone).  
- Left AIC pelvis days: hemibridge / adductor pull-back / right glute max sidelying family → then frontal-plane single-leg control.  
- PEC days: wall-supported reach, 90-90 in passive FA IR with balloon, modified all-four belly lift - bilateral extension bias first.  
- Patho PEC flags → collaborate clinically; don't "progress squat depth" off a 0" reach with + PART.  
- Keep reference centers in coaching: left abs, left ischial seat, left heel, right arch (Integration language shared across intros).

Open the full reference for full hierarchy steps, manual technique pages, and Hruska Adduction Lift appendix notes.
