    errors.push(`${p}: must equal ${safeQuote(schema.const)}, got ${safeQuote(value)}`);
  }
  if (hasOwn(schema, "enum") && !schema.enum.some((allowed) => deepEqual(value, allowed))) {
    const allowed = schema.enum.map(safeQuote).join(", ");
    errors.push(`${p}: invalid value ${safeQuote(value)} (expected one of ${allowed})`);

  if (hasOwn(schema, "type") && typeOf(value) !== schema.type && !(schema.type === "integer" && typeOf(value) === "number" && Number.isInteger(value))) {
    errors.push(`${p}: expected ${schema.type}, got ${typeOf(value)}`);
    return;
  }

  if (typeOf(value) === "object") {
    for (const req of hasOwn(schema, "required") ? schema.required : []) {
      if (!hasOwn(value, req)) errors.push(`${p}: missing required field ${safeQuote(req)}`);
    }
    for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {
      if (hasOwn(schema, "properties") && hasOwn(schema.properties, key)) {
        validate(value[key], schema.properties[key], propertyPath(p, key), errors);
      } else if (hasOwn(schema, "additionalProperties") && schema.additionalProperties === false) {
        errors.push(`${p}: unexpected field ${safeQuote(key)}`);

  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    if (hasOwn(schema, "minItems") && value.length < schema.minItems) {
      errors.push(`${p}: must have at least ${schema.minItems} item(s), got ${value.length}`);

    if (hasOwn(schema, "uniqueItems") && schema.uniqueItems === true) {

      let setBytes = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i++) {
        let canonical;
        try {
          canonical = canonicalKey(value[i]);
        } catch (error) {
          errors.push(`${p}[${i}]: ${error.message}`);
          break;
        }
        if (seen.has(canonical.key)) {
          errors.push(`${p}: items must be unique; duplicate at index ${i}`);
          continue;
        }
        setBytes += canonical.bytes;
        if (setBytes > LIMITS.uniqueSetBytes) {
          errors.push(`${p}: canonical uniqueness set exceeds ${LIMITS.uniqueSetBytes} byte limit`);

        seen.add(canonical.key);

    if (hasOwn(schema, "items")) {
      value.forEach((item, index) => validate(item, schema.items, `${p}[${index}]`, errors));

  if (typeof value === "string") {
    if (hasOwn(schema, "minLength") && codePointLength(value) < schema.minLength) {
      errors.push(`${p}: must have at least ${schema.minLength} character(s)`);
    }
    if (schema.visibleContent === true) {
      if (!hasValidUnicodeScalarValues(value)) {

      } else if (!VISIBLE_CONTENT.test(value)) {

    if (hasOwn(schema, "pattern") && !(new RegExp(schema.pattern).test(value))) {

function collectUnchecked(value, schema, p) {
  const errors = createErrorList();

function collect(value, schema, p = "$data") {

function collectFindingSemanticErrors(findings) {
  const errors = createErrorList();
  if (!Array.isArray(findings)) return errors;

  findings.forEach((finding, index) => {

    if (!finding || typeof finding !== "object" || Array.isArray(finding)) return;
    const base = `$[${index}]`;

    if (hasOwn(finding, "fingerprint") && typeof finding.fingerprint === "string") {
      if (fingerprints.has(finding.fingerprint)) {

      }
      previousFingerprint = finding.fingerprint;
    }

    for (const field of ["trace", "evidence"]) {
      if (!hasOwn(finding, field) || !Array.isArray(finding[field])) continue;
      finding[field].forEach((entry, entryIndex) => {
        if (!entry || typeof entry !== "object" || Array.isArray(entry)) return;
        if (hasOwn(entry, "line") && (!Number.isInteger(entry.line) || entry.line < 1)) {
          errors.push(`${base}.${field}[${entryIndex}].line: must be a positive integer`);
        }
        if (hasOwn(entry, "file") && !isSafeRelativeSourcePath(entry.file)) {
          errors.push(`${base}.${field}[${entryIndex}].file: must be a safe repository-relative source path`);
        }

    }
    if (finding.remediation && Array.isArray(finding.remediation.code_changes)) {
      finding.remediation.code_changes.forEach((change, changeIndex) => {
        if (change && hasOwn(change, "file_name") && !isSafeRelativeSourcePath(change.file_name)) {
          errors.push(`${base}.remediation.code_changes[${changeIndex}].file_name: must be a safe repository-relative source path`);

    }

    if (Array.isArray(finding.trace) && finding.trace.length === 1) {
      const kind = finding.trace[0] && finding.trace[0].kind;
      if (kind !== "entrypoint" && kind !== "sink") {
        errors.push(`${base}.trace[0].kind: a one-line trace must be "entrypoint" or "sink"`);
      }
    } else if (Array.isArray(finding.trace) && finding.trace.length > 1) {
      const last = finding.trace.length - 1;
      if (finding.trace[0] && finding.trace[0].kind !== "entrypoint") {
        errors.push(`${base}.trace[0].kind: must be "entrypoint", got ${safeQuote(finding.trace[0].kind)}`);
      }
      if (finding.trace[last] && finding.trace[last].kind !== "sink") {
        errors.push(`${base}.trace[${last}].kind: must be "sink", got ${safeQuote(finding.trace[last].kind)}`);
      }
      for (let traceIndex = 1; traceIndex < last; traceIndex++) {
        if (finding.trace[traceIndex] && finding.trace[traceIndex].kind !== "propagation") {
          errors.push(`${base}.trace[${traceIndex}].kind: must be "propagation", got ${safeQuote(finding.trace[traceIndex].kind)}`);

    const verdict = finding.verdict;
    if (verdict === "confirmed") {
      for (const forbidden of ["claimed_root_cause", "blockers", "validation_plan", "reason"]) {

      if (!finding.remediation || typeof finding.remediation !== "object" || typeof finding.remediation.strategy !== "string" || !hasVisibleProse(finding.remediation.strategy)) {

      const impact = finding.severity && finding.severity.impact && finding.severity.impact.score;

      if (hasOwn(finding, "severity")) errors.push(`${base}: needs_validation finding must not contain "severity"`);

  const schemaErrors = collectSchemaErrors(schema);
  if (schemaErrors.length > 0) return schemaErrors;
  const limitErrors = collectDataLimitErrors(findings, "$");
  if (limitErrors.length > 0) return limitErrors;
  const errors = collectUnchecked(findings, schema, "$");
  if (errors.length < LIMITS.validationErrors) {
    errors.push(...collectFindingSemanticErrors(findings));
  }

  const errors = collectSchemaErrors(schema);
  if (errors.length > 0) throw new Error(`unsupported or invalid report schema:\n${errors.join("\n")}`);
  return schema;

function readFileWithinLimit(file) {
  const noFollow = fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW;
  const nonBlock = fs.constants.O_NONBLOCK;
  if (!Number.isInteger(noFollow) || noFollow === 0 || !Number.isInteger(nonBlock) || nonBlock === 0) {
    throw new SafeInputError("OS no-follow and nonblocking input protection is unavailable");
  }

  let descriptor;
  try {
    descriptor = fs.openSync(file, fs.constants.O_RDONLY | noFollow | nonBlock);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error && (error.code === "ELOOP" || error.code === "EMLINK")) {
      throw new SafeInputError("input must not be a symlink");
    }
    throw error;
  }
  try {
    const stat = fs.fstatSync(descriptor);
    if (!stat.isFile()) {
      throw new SafeInputError("input must be a regular file");
    }
    if (stat.size > LIMITS.inputBytes) {
      throw new SafeInputError(`input exceeds ${LIMITS.inputBytes} byte limit`);
    }

    const chunks = [];
    const buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(64 * 1024);
    let bytesRead = 0;
    while (true) {
      const count = fs.readSync(descriptor, buffer, 0, buffer.length, null);
      if (count === 0) break;
      bytesRead += count;
      if (bytesRead > LIMITS.inputBytes) {
        throw new SafeInputError(`input exceeds ${LIMITS.inputBytes} byte limit`);
      }
      chunks.push(Buffer.from(buffer.subarray(0, count)));
    }
    try {
      return UTF8_DECODER.decode(Buffer.concat(chunks, bytesRead));
    } catch {
      throw new SafeInputError("input is not valid UTF-8");
    }
  } finally {
    fs.closeSync(descriptor);
  }
}

function enforceJsonTextLimits(contents) {
  const containers = [];
  let inString = false;
  let escaped = false;

  function markArrayItem() {
    const container = containers[containers.length - 1];
    if (!container || container.type !== "array" || !container.expectsItem) return;
    container.expectsItem = false;
    container.items++;
    if (container.items > LIMITS.arrayItems) {
      throw new JsonStructureError(`input exceeds ${LIMITS.arrayItems} item array limit`);
    }
  }

  for (let index = 0; index < contents.length; index++) {
    const character = contents[index];
    if (inString) {
      if (escaped) {
        escaped = false;
      } else if (character === "\\") {
        escaped = true;
      } else if (character === "\"") {
        inString = false;
      }
      continue;
    }

    if (character === "\"") {
      markArrayItem();
      inString = true;
    } else if (character === "[" || character === "{") {
      markArrayItem();
      if (containers.length >= LIMITS.nestingDepth) {
        throw new JsonStructureError(`input exceeds ${LIMITS.nestingDepth} level nesting depth limit`);
      }
      containers.push({
        type: character === "[" ? "array" : "object",
        expectsItem: character === "[",
        items: 0,
      });
    } else if (character === "]" || character === "}") {
      containers.pop();
    } else if (character === ",") {
      const container = containers[containers.length - 1];
      if (container && container.type === "array") container.expectsItem = true;
    } else if (!/\s/.test(character)) {
      markArrayItem();
    }
  }
}

function run(file) {
  if (!file) {
    console.error("Usage: node validate-findings.cjs <path-to-findings.json>");
    return 1;
  }

  let schema;
  try {
    schema = loadSchema(path.join(__dirname, "report-schema.json"));
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Failed to load report-schema.json:", error.message);
    return 1;
  }

  let contents;
  try {
    contents = readFileWithinLimit(file);
  } catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof SafeInputError ? error.message : "input could not be opened or read safely";
    console.error(`Failed to read findings JSON: ${reason}`);
    return 1;
  }

  try {
    enforceJsonTextLimits(contents);
  } catch (error) {
    const reason = error instanceof JsonStructureError ? error.message : "invalid JSON structure";
    console.error(`Failed to parse findings JSON: ${reason}`);
    return 1;
  }

  let findings;
  try {
    findings = JSON.parse(contents);
  } catch {
    console.error("Failed to parse findings JSON: invalid JSON syntax");
    return 1;
  }

  let errors;
  try {
    errors = validateDocument(findings, schema);
  } catch {
    console.error("Failed to validate findings JSON: unexpected validation error");
    return 1;
  }
  for (const message of errors) console.error("ERROR:", escapeUnsafeDiagnosticCharacters(message));
  if (errors.length > 0) {
    const cap = errors.length === LIMITS.validationErrors ? `; output capped at ${LIMITS.validationErrors}` : "";
    console.error(`FAIL: ${errors.length} validation error(s)${cap}`);
    return 1;
  }
  console.log(`PASS [param] ${findings.length} findings valid`);
  return 0;
}

  LIMITS,
  PATH_FORBIDDEN_CHARACTER,
  UNSAFE_DIAGNOSTIC_CHARACTER,
  VISIBLE_CONTENT,
  WINDOWS_RESERVED_COMPONENT,
  collect,
  collectFindingSemanticErrors,
  collectSchemaErrors,
  hasVisibleProse,
  isSafeRelativeSourcePath,
  validateDocument,
};

if (require.main === module) process.exit(run(process.argv[2]));

skills.description: Use when the user wants an SEO audit: Search Console, indexing, on-page, AI traffic, scored findings delivered like an agency deck - not a dump.
skills.instructions:
---
name: SEO Audit
description: >-
  Use when the user wants an SEO audit: Search Console, indexing, on-page, AI
  traffic, scored findings delivered like an agency deck - not a dump.
---
A scored, prioritized SEO report from LIVE data. Every finding cites a real query, page, or fetched element. Missing source: say so. Never invent impressions, position, or clicks.

## Connector
If the Ryze AI connector is missing, stop. Add `https://connector.get-ryze.ai/mcp` (docs: https://www.get-ryze.ai/how-to-connect-claude-to-google-meta-ads-mcp). Wait.

List connections first. No Search Console → say what it unlocks (queries, rankings) and offer a reduced audit (on-page + fetched pages). Do not stall. GA4 connected → rank by money and pull AI-referral traffic. No GA4 → skip that slice, do not fake it.

## Flow
1. Scope. Confirm the GSC property. Two windows: last 28 days vs prior 28. State property + window in one line before digging.
2. Young site. GSC near-empty → say it once. Weight indexing, on-page of key pages, competitor/keyword gap. Do not pad empty sections.
3. Queries. High impressions + weak CTR (title/meta). Striking distance 11-20, ranked by impressions. Branded vs non-branded. Decay vs prior window. One device pull, one country pull.
4. Pages. Top landings by clicks - are these the pages the business wants? Impression-heavy / click-poor. Single-query pages (thin coverage). Join GA4 conversions if present so money reorders the list.
5. Indexing. Sitemap summary. Inspect 2-3 key URLs (submitted-not-indexed, crawled-not-indexed).
6. On-page. Fetch at most 5 pages. For each: title + meta present/unique/aligned to the query it actually ranks for; one h1; canonical; structure.
7. AI visibility. Only with GA4: ChatGPT / Perplexity / Gemini sessions, landings, trend. Its own beat, not a footnote.
8. Score 0-100, honest: indexing 20, query capture 20, on-page 20, coverage 15, technical/off-page 15, trend 10. 90+ excellent, 70-89 good, 50-69 needs work, <50 critical. A flattering score kills the follow-up.

Cap the run: two GSC windows, one device, one country, 5 page fetches, one AI pull. Depth is analysis, not more pulls.

## How it reads
Pick ONE visual identity and keep it (Bold Signal / Electric Studio / Dark Botanical / Vintage Editorial). Cover title is the conclusion, not "SEO Report". One idea per beat. Numbers first. Section titles are claims: "Pricing sits at position 11 on 41k impressions".

Lead with the score and three opportunities ranked by click/revenue impact. Close with P0 / P1 and expected impact.

## Writes
Offer the top on-page fixes one at a time, exact new title/meta. Never write a CMS, sitemap, or live page without a yes on that change.

skills.name: sheet-write-readback
skills.description: Use whenever you write to a spreadsheet (Google Sheets directly or through Zapier) or keep a running total in one. A success response is not proof the row is right: read it back, never retry blind, and treat the sheet as truth.
skills.instructions:
---
name: Sheet write read-back
description: >-
  Use whenever you write to a spreadsheet (Google Sheets directly or through
  Zapier) or keep a running total in one. A success response is not proof the
  row is right: read it back, never retry blind, and treat the sheet as truth.
---
# Sheet write read-back

## Before a write (prospect rows)
Check for duplicates first: `python3 /home/box/agent-data/shared/scripts/chief/sheet_readback.py --prewrite --rows --key "Email Address" --intended <file> --readback <current sheet export>`. If it reports two matching rows, do not write; flag a possible duplicate.

## After every write
1. Save what you meant to write (JSON of cell/range to value, or the row) as a file. Re-read the row or cell you just wrote, looking it up by its key (email, row number, or cell address), not by trusting the write response, and save that re-read as a file.
2. Run `python3 /home/box/agent-data/shared/scripts/chief/sheet_readback.py --intended <file> --readback <file>` (add `--rows --key "Email Address"` for prospect rows; `--help` lists options). It compares name, email, phone, Contact Date, Stage, or the cell values, ignoring formatting-only differences.
3. Say "written and verified" only on exit 0. Any MISMATCH, MISSING, DUPLICATE, or NOT READ BACK line is a failure.

## On a mismatch or an error
- Mismatch: stop writing to that sheet for this run, and flag it to the owner or the user with the row, the field, what you wrote, and what you read back.
- Write error or timeout: look the row up first. Retry at most once, and only if the write is truly absent. If the second try fails or the lookup is unclear, stop and flag. Never loop retries.
- Two rows match one person or key: do not write. Flag a possible duplicate.

## Source of truth
- The sheet is the source of truth. Side files, logs, or memory notes that track the same thing are helpers; when they disagree with the sheet, the sheet wins and the difference gets flagged.
- Running totals: never add to a total you computed yourself. Read the sheet's own SUM or cells, then report.
- Counts parsed from chat: treat "add N" or "N more" as an increment only when the wording is explicit. A number that could be a total ("12 so far", "12 from Saturday to now") is ambiguous: ask before writing.

## Reconcile
For any sheet fed from messages (chat counts, form emails), run a recount once a day or once a week: re-count from the source for the period, compare with the sheet, and post any differences. Silent only when they match.

# Siff + Zatsiorsky programming rules (Ryne-approved 2026-10-05)

Full reference with page refs: `/workspace/books/strength/strength-key-ideas.md`. Achieve trains athletes in the gym only. There's no pool training, so skip pool-based tools (drag suits, paddles, in-water work).

## Approved rules

1. **Check the explosive strength deficit (ESD) before picking the block emphasis.** ESD is how much of an athlete's max strength they can't express in a fast sport movement: ESD % = 100 x (max force - force in the sport action) / max force. If ESD is well under 50%, more max strength still pays. Around 50% or more, shift volume toward rate of force development, speed-strength, and plyos. Zatsiorsky's measure: peak force in the explosive sport action divided against max force in the most favorable slow condition, e.g. peak force on the shot vs bench 1RM per arm (Zat p. 27-28, 116). On Achieve plates the closest proxy is DSI (jump peak force vs isometric peak force). Siff's separate field check is squat jump vs countermovement jump (Siff p. 9-10).
2. **Progress jumps from force plate data, not a fixed calendar.** The general order is ordinary jumps, then barbell strength, then loaded jumps, then depth jumps, but the plates decide when an athlete moves up. Change the main power method when the plates stall, and use roughly 12-18 weeks on one method as the outer limit. (Siff p. 287-289, 295; Zat p. 128)
3. **Gate depth jumps.** Require months of barbell work and ordinary jumps first. Set drop height with the heel test (the highest drop where the heels aren't forced to the ground). No vests or cords. Use them 1-2 times a week, for at most 1-2 blocks in a row. In season, use one exposure every 7-14 days and none in the last 10 days before a key meet. (Siff p. 221, 273-274, 279-280; Zat p. 128-129)
4. **Progress reactive work by raising the drop height, not the load.** Keep ground contact short, like a hot surface, and don't coach stuck landings as reactive training. (Siff p. 221-222, 266; Zat p. 125-128)
5. **Depth jumps go after heavy strength work in the same session, never before.** Resistance work followed by depth jumps beat depth jumps alone. Ordinary jumps and other speed-strength work still go early, before strength work, while the athlete is fresh. (Siff p. 275, 288)
6. **Use the Rule of 60% on accessory volume.** The lightest week or day carries about 60% of the volume of the heaviest, and load fluctuates rather than rising every week. (Siff p. 84, 90-91, 316; Zat p. 97)
7. **Primary lifts can carry over between programs. Change secondary and tertiary exercises every program.** (Zat p. 97, 103, 155-156)
8. **Expect results 2-6 weeks after a hard block (about 4 weeks on average).** Retest after the unload, not at the end of the loading weeks, and don't stack a new hard block before the delayed effect shows. (Zat p. 98, 104; Siff p. 292)
9. **In-season sessions run 35-45 minutes, with 2 short heavy sessions a week to hold strength.** At the end of a taper, right before competition, sessions drop to 35 minutes. Don't drop to moderate-only loading for longer than about a month. (Zat p. 77, 97, 104; Siff p. 316)
13. **For youth under about 14:** no near-max overhead lifts, low-back work at 10 or more reps, no 1RM testing in the first weeks (estimate it from a 5-6RM), and at least 2 sessions a week to hold gains. (Zat p. 198-204; Siff p. 323-324)
14. **For adults over about 60:** add one power slot at 30-40% 1RM using exercises with no deceleration, keep sets around 3 reps short of failure, and space very heavy days 3-7 or more days apart. (Zat p. 219-225)
15. **Start every new adult client under the Statute of Fitness Limitations.** Lift one limit at a time, based on coach technique rating plus athlete RPE. (Siff p. 428)

## Rejected

- Rules 10 and 11, swim pool tools and timing recovery around pool doubles. Achieve does no pool training.
- Rule 12, weekly readiness triage plus monthly test battery.

# Silent run heartbeat

A quiet run is only trustworthy if you can show what it checked. An expired connector, a wrong query, or a missed run looks exactly like "nothing new".

## Every run, including silent ones
Append one line to the routine's own log (a file in your memory or workspace, one line per run):

`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM CT | window <from> to <to> | sources <list> | items seen <n> | items acted on <n> | errors <none or short text>`

Use the time zone America/Chicago. Never put secret values in the log.

## Search windows
Search from the last processed item (id or timestamp saved after the previous good run), not a fixed "last 1 day". That way a missed or late run is caught up, not skipped.

## Alert instead of staying silent when
1. A source that is normally busy in this window returns 0 items (set the expected floor in the routine, for example "0 form emails in 7 days").
2. The previous run did not happen, ran late past its window, or did not finish (no log line for it).
3. Any connector or API call returned an error, a sign-in or re-auth prompt, a partial page, or a warning.
4. A count drops sharply from the last run (for example a sheet or list shrinking by more than 10%).

The alert is one short message to the user or the owning bot: what was checked, what came back, and the likely cause. Then stay quiet until it changes.

## Stop condition
On a connector error or a partial read, do not overwrite saved state (snapshots, cursors, last-id files). Keep the last good state and alert.

# Strength Coach program output

## Default (locked 2026-10-02 by Ryne; Programming room gone 2026-11-05)

Coach owns the wrap with Ryne. On a normal athlete ask you post the **final** prescription in chat after specialists have sent their notes.

**Flow (normal asks):**
1. Get the athlete context from Asana (or Ryne).
2. Wait for **one private note each** from specialists in order: **Hawkin → PRI → S&C Research** (Research only if needed; they may stay silent).
3. Then post **exactly one** final wrap in Coach's chat with Ryne, incorporating those notes plus your expertise (dose, exercises, direction).

No duplicate wraps.

**ONE message per athlete ask** from you. If you revise, **one** revise post only - not a duplicate of the original plus a revise.

**Do not write full Day 1 / Day 2 programs in chat** unless Ryne asks for a full draft. He writes TrainHeroic.

Talk like a coach. Plain English. No gymspeak pile-on.

```
{Name}

Force Plates
- Main finding
- Main finding
- Main finding (as many as the plates warrant)
- Programming recommendations based on findings:

S&C research (when applicable)
- Article
  - Why it's relevant
- Article
  - Why it's relevant
- Recommendation based on findings

PRI
- Warm-up technique based on client information
  - Why
- Possible other technique to be used near the end of the program along with core and tertiary exercises

Strength Coach
- Specific programming recommendation
- Specific programming recommendation
- Specific programming recommendation
- Specific programming recommendation (count flexes)
```

### Force Plates language (locked 2026-10-02)
- Never say **soft** (or soft day) for plate output. Use **higher / lower / plateau** with dates.
- Lead with **trend** when Hawkin gives one.
- **Swimmers:** put **SJ next to CMJ** (SJ often primary); mirror Hawkin’s trend line.
- Keep curve/mechanics findings in plain words; numbers and dates fine.

### Strength Coach section = the final call (not a recap)
Specialist sections can keep plate/PRI/research findings and their own recs. **Strength Coach must synthesize into your prescription**, not restate what they said. Include as relevant:
- Programming direction for this block (what wins this week/month)
- Training volume / density (days/week, jump contacts, how hard to push)
- Specific exercise ideas (names he uses) driven by plates + PRI + Asana + research
- Session shape hints (e.g. warm-up → jump quality → strength pairs → serratus/core) without a full A-H writeup unless asked
- Hard stops / gates folded into the call

### Rules
- Force Plates / PRI / Research content comes from the specialists' **notes** - synthesize into the sections; do not invent plates, papers, or PRI techniques.
- Omit **S&C research** entirely when Research was silent.
- Omit **PRI** if they were not in the loop / nothing PRI-relevant.
- No keep/swap/drop. No NEW/KEEP tags. No walls of text.
- Number of bullets depends on the athlete and what you have to share.

## Full draft (only if he asks)

Only then use a scannable Day 1 / Day 2 layout with sheet names, sets/reps, and start loads.

skills.instructions:
---
name: Superpower narrow vs wide programming
description: >-
  Use when classifying or programming Narrow/elastic vs Wide/muscle-driven
  athletes (ISA, CMJ/four-jump strategy, Superpower vs Kryptonite phases and
  dose by training age).
---
# Superpower: Narrow/elastic vs Wide/muscle programming

**Source:** Hunter Eisenhower, SimpliFaster (2024-04-15) - *How to Train Narrow & Elastic-Driven Athletes vs. Wide & Muscle-Driven*. Full clip: `/home/box/agent-data/shared/sc-reference/superpower-narrow-elastic-vs-wide-muscle.md`

**Cross-links:** [CMJ force-time curve shape classification](sand-workflow:cmj-force-time-curve-shape-classification) · Hawkin Dynamics for plates · [Isometrics programming guide](sand-workflow:isometrics-programming-guide) when rigidity/iso is the elastic base · house order [Athlete program design guidelines](sand-workflow:athlete-program-design-guidelines)

Eisenhower’s frame: structure (ISA) biases **Superpowers** vs **Kryptonites**. Dose kryptonite early (raise the floor), flip to superpower closer to season (raise the ceiling). Spectrum, not binary - place the athlete, then dose by **timing + training age**.

---

## 1. Classify the athlete

### Infrasternal angle (structure)
Cited via Conor Harris:
- **Wide** ISA ≈ **>110°**
- **Narrow** ISA ≈ **<100°**
- In between = spectrum; extreme examples often readable without a goniometer (rib-cage width).

| | **Narrow** | **Wide** |
|---|---|---|
| Typical bias | External rotation; feet more **supination**; more A-P space, less frontal | Internal rotation / compression; feet more **pronation**; more frontal space, less A-P |
| Stance preference | Staggered / **split**; avoid grinding bilateral IR | **Bilateral**; less space for split |
| Movement strategy | **Elastic** - muscle more isometric; tendons stretch/recoil (“free energy”) | **Muscular** - classic ecc→con; high force, slower / costlier |
| Sport fit (examples) | Guards, springy skill - short GCT | Linemen / “force over time” tasks |
| Coach bias risk | Overdosed all year on powerlifting = kryptonite | Feels natural to most S&C coaches |

### Force-plate strategy (how > jump height alone)

**CMJ (hands-on-hips):**
- **Muscular / Wide-leaning:** deeper countermovement; slower time to takeoff; **bimodal** F-T curve (peaks at end of braking + start of propulsion). Continuum: bimodal **secondary** (most muscular) → bimodal **primary** (mid) → **unimodal** (most elastic).
- **Elastic / Narrow-leaning:** shallower CM; faster TTT; **unimodal** sharp peak.

**Four-jump / multi-rebound** (prefer over single drop jump for rhythm/coordination):
- Similar RSI can hide strategy: Wides often **longer GCT + higher jump**; Narrows **shorter GCT**.
- Measures efficiency of the elastic system under repeated contacts.

Do not classify from jump height alone. Pair ISA + CMJ shape + four-jump strategy. Hand full Hawkin pulls to Hawkin Dynamics; use this skill for programming bias once classified.

---

## 2. Annual logic: Kryptonite → Superpower

| Phase | When | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| **Kryptonite** | Earlier off-season (time before competition) | Build the other archetype’s qualities; raise the **floor**. Short-term KPI dips OK. |
| **Superpower** | Later off-season → into preseason | Dose native strengths hard; raise the **ceiling**. Concurrent sport-volume resiliency. |

**Training-age dosage (example 8-week off-season):**
- Young Narrow: kryptonite ~**6**/8 weeks (foundation)
- Veteran Narrow: kryptonite ~**2**/8 weeks (then maximize elastic ceiling)
- Maintain small doses of the “other” means year-round so the floor doesn’t collapse
- Never “peak” everyone with bilateral 1RM PR week right before season - outdated for elastic types

Speed: still progress max velocity + repeat sprint (e.g. 10×10 Hansen) **regardless** of bucket; later individualize speed by archetype.

---

## 3. Kryptonite menus

### Narrow / elastic - kryptonite (train more like a Wide)
- Highest yearly dose of **traditional bilateral** loading + rising intensity
- Deadlifts, bilateral press/pull, deep bilateral squat patterns as appropriate
- Expect: CMJ JH may drop from training stress, but *how* shifts - greater CM depth, slightly slower TTT, unimodal → **slightly more bimodal**; four-jump: ↑ GCT and ↑ JH (RSI maybe flat) = more muscular strategy
- Still not *only* these weeks in the year - just the peak dose

### Wide / muscular - kryptonite (train more like a Narrow)
- Strip bilateral high-intensity; challenge **force in short time / short ROM / light loads**
- Progress **extensive plyo** volume; unilateral lower + upper; rotation (crawl, roll, gymnastic-type)
- Expect: JH may fall faster (OK) if **TTT ↓** and CM **shallower**; four-jump: **↓ GCT** even if JH flat

**Phase goal:** Narrows behave more Wide-like and Wides more Narrow-like before the flip.

---

## 4. Superpower menus

### Narrow / elastic - superpower
- Avoid high-intensity bilateral that forces prolonged IR + heavy compression (bilateral U+L)
- Prefer **staggered / split** lower body
- **Speed of movement > load intensity**
- Upper body: rotation + freedom
- Plyos: more elastic variation (e.g. SL approach jumps) vs standstill vertical only
- Keep **some** muscular means; majority elastic

**Plate targets:** ↑ JH, ↓ TTT, shallower CM, sharp unimodal. Four-jump RSI ↑ mainly via **↓ GCT**, secondarily ↑ JH.

### Wide / muscular - superpower
- Return to **higher intensity bilateral** lower + upper
- Faster movements: allow more time to produce force; load **slightly heavier** than Narrow superpower group
- “Peak” feel: 1-3RM near season OK for this archetype (physio + psych)
- Still build plyo volume for sport resiliency even if not their native love

**Plate targets:** ↑ JH, ↓ TTT, **deeper** CM (ideally: fast load + hard brake so TTT still improves with more depth). Curve: bimodal secondary → primary, or primary → unimodal as elastic qualities catch up. Four-jump RSI ↑ mainly via **↑ JH**, GCT steady or slightly better.

---

## 5. Achieve translation

1. **Classify** with ISA (when known) + Hawkin CMJ shape + multi-rebound if available - ask Hawkin; don’t invent curves.
2. **Early block / young training age:** bias kryptonite (raise floor). **Late block / veteran elastic:** bias superpower (raise ceiling).
3. In Programming drafts: name the bias in Direction (“Narrow/elastic superpower: split stance, speed, elastic plyos; maintain floor with light bilateral”) rather than dumping both menus equally.
4. Swimmers / overhead: still honor overhead rules and [Swim dryland programming](sand-workflow:swim-dryland-programming); ISA bias modulates stance, plyo type, and bilateral dose - it does not override scap/PRI constraints.
5. Force-time continuum language matches Achieve CMJ guide: secondary bimodal ↔ primary bimodal ↔ unimodal. Use both skills together.

## Anti-patterns
- Year-round powerlifting peak for Narrow/elastic athletes
- Calling skill athletes “soft” for avoiding heavy bilateral IR/compression
- Programming only from absolute JH without strategy metrics
- Treating every athlete as Wide because that’s what most coaches prefer to train

# Swim dryland programming

Full notes: `/home/box/agent-data/agents/0c56f311-56b5-4ded-ae36-22f03da7a160/memory/reference/strength-conditioning-programming-for-swimmers.txt`

**Separate skills (do not merge):**
- [PRI Swimming An In-Depth Look](sand-workflow:pri-swimming-in-depth) - PRI pathomechanics / PEC-AIC-BC
- [PRI shoulder pain prescription](sand-workflow:pri-shoulder-pain-prescription) - Advanced Integration bicipital vs impingement technique menus
- [Swim turn and start ISO angles](sand-workflow:swim-turn-and-start-iso-angles) - pool-transfer isometric angles
- [FRC progressions and prescriptions](sand-workflow:frc-progressions-and-prescriptions) - CARs / PAILs / swimmer hovers / ERR
- House session order: [Athlete program design guidelines](sand-workflow:athlete-program-design-guidelines)

This skill owns **stroke-specific dryland bias, starts/turns/UW, scapular rules, shoulder pain fixes, and in-season constraints**.

---

## Always-on swimmer rules

1. **Scapulae / neck**
   - R scapula → R lower trap + R triceps
   - L scapula → L serratus (depression / protraction / rib-cage retraction)
   - Every program needs a **squat-and-reach** somehow (seat scapulae on rib cage, quiet neck). Cue **reach forward, not shrug**.
     - Wall supported reach → band-resisted wall reach → squatting bar reach → squatting bar reverse reach
   - UT / neck inhibition: rib-cage IR, SCM balance

2. **Streamline triad** (fly, breast, sprint free, UW): full **shoulder flexion + hip extension + plantar flexion**. Normal PF ROM **40-50°**. Much "toe point" = **midfoot flexion**.

3. **Catch pain** = over-active lat + under-active subscap. Impingement theme: better **R triceps + L ZOA**, lat inhibition, rib expansion, **R HG IR** (R scap retraction).

4. **Straight-arm press down** = key for fly + free. Straight-elbow shoulder extension helps all strokes.

5. **Rolling + rotation:** MSR (and lumbar-locked rotation / ISA as needed). **Prone↔supine rolling** is a primary corrective for free + back body roll. Back needs ~**30°** roll relative to water.

6. **Core:** ~**2** core exercises per workout across the 4 categories; progress toward stability **with moving limbs**.

7. **In-season / within 2 weeks of a key meet:** minimize slideboard/glider + eccentrics; favor concentric; **no new exercises** (soreness).

8. **Season shoulder math:** IR strength rises more than ER over a season → IR:ER drifts. Bias ER / scap control and don't only feed IR. (JSR: high-school swimmers over a competitive season.)

---

## Volume bias by stroke / event

| Population | Loading / volume bias |
|---|---|
| Fly | Less bilateral; **upper > lower** volume likely; still train legs for kick/starts/turns |
| Back | More bilateral; **upper > lower** likely; slightly more leg than free (kick volume) |
| Breast | Less bilateral; **upper ≈ lower** (kick-driven but multi-event athletes) |
| Free sprint | More bilateral; **legs + jumps priority**; more RT volume than distance |
| Free distance | More bilateral; **upper > lower** likely; endurance / circuits; connecting U+L |

---

## By stroke (prescription lens)

### Butterfly
- PF/DF screen; glutes + leave bilateral extension (sagittal / QL / lat inhibition) if dolphin LBP
- Straight-arm press down; prone HA via **swimmer hovers**, HA ball drops, functional squat w/ low trap

### Backstroke
- Trunk rotation for deep catch (palm down); R HA (L if needed) via:
  - L sidelying resisted serratus punch + R trunk rotation
  - L sidelying L flexed FA adduction + R glute max + R trunk rotation
- Rib integration / sidelying Swiss ball + R apical expansion for roll
- Watch pull-phase hyperextension / anterior glide / impingement

### Breaststroke
- Tall kneeling core (OH reach, anti-rotation, MB OH throws) for straight-hip + stability
- **PADT negative bilaterally** required for breast kick - else ipsilateral LBP / knee / groin
- Knee flexion **with straight hips**: Swiss ball / slideboard / TRX curls, Nordics, GHD, SHELC
- Breaststroker’s knee often **missing hip IR** → IR-bias SL squat etc.
- Assess: hip IR/ER, extension + adduction drop, prone hip ext, PF/DF

### Freestyle
- Full hip ext without lumbar cheat (prone table); PRI all-4 SL R glute max; leave extension posture
- Trunk rotation for DPS / early catch / high elbow; R HA (same L-sidelying pair as back)
- Neck rotation for bilateral breath (L abs + R chest wall themes)

**Sprint free:** kick + vertical/horizontal jump culture (starts/turns ~leg-driven); less shoulder roll than distance; own top speed in first 2 strokes (straight-arm extension); higher RT volume; streamline.

**Distance free:** more shoulder roll / stroke length; endurance over max strength; lower volume; TGU / contralateral offset connectors; triceps may matter for reach-glide rhythm.

---

## Starts

- Spinal flexion to grab block: toe touch; PEC / paraspinal inhibition (often pairs with limited OH for streamline)
- PF + **first ray** strength matter
- Horizontal / split-stance power bank: staggered broad jump (± band); weighted squat jump (± bands); split-stance weight slides (arm drive); GHD; DB step-up jump; staggered trap-bar DL; staggered BB hip thrust; KB swing as horizontal option
- Explosive split-stance: sandbag hang clean → step/box; trap-bar high pull; 1-arm DB snatch ± step; SL RDL → hang clean; rotational reverse lunge → hang clean; sled 1-push / multi / jump from split
- Backstroke start: MB OH scoop toss or scoop behind
- FFE split stance broad / box jump; box jump with front foot on DC blocks

## Turns

- Push-off knee **110-120°** (SSC): mid-pause squats, paused box jumps, heavy partials in that range, hurdle / depth jumps, bands/chains
- Compact flip = spinal flexion (same PEC/toe-touch theme as starts)
- Season: full-depth early → bias **½ squat / 110-120°** closer to championship meets

## Underwater / kick

- +10° PF ≈ +16 N on dolphin downsweep (~66% peak force at feet)
- UW breath-hold often limiting; deep pre-race breathing may help 50/100 free
- Strong up-kick = glutes + hammies; GHD useful for starts + kick

---

## Shoulder pain menus (PRI-named)

Full Advanced Integration banks: [PRI shoulder pain prescription](sand-workflow:pri-shoulder-pain-prescription). Short Achieve list below.

**General shoulder pain**
1. Lat hang (standing lat inhibition 1)
2. L sidelying weighted R HG HA + R FA ER (R low trap / R triceps 4) - R scap retraction + L IO → R HG IR theme
3. Supine resisted R HG IR + L HG ER (R low trap / R triceps 16) - R towel wedge, towel under L elbow; keep L ZOA/PME/IO
4. L SL resisted R HG IR (R subscap 2) - L ZOA + L trunk rotation + R HG IR

**Impingement:** abs exhale + stay contracted on inhale (rib expansion); lat inhibition; R low trap + R triceps.

**Biceps tendonitis:** R upper trunk rotation; R apical expansion; R subscap + lat inhibition. Same L sidelying serratus punch + R trunk rotation as HA driver.

**L shoulder pain (often MDI):** treat as bilateral / longer course. After repositioning → L posterior mediastinum expansion (reach + L abs); may need L pec inhibition. AF belly lift reach; modified AFBL pad under L hand; long seated alternating crossovers; AF belly lift.

**Long seated supported press downs** (R iliacus/psoas **or** abs) - useful when UT / FHP / bicipital / rounded shoulders / flat back / tight calves / anterior scalenes themes stack.

---

## Dryland performance screens (optional standards)

Candidate weakness map: front squat velocity, **1RM pull-up**, trap-bar DL, **non-CMJ**, standing broad jump.

Published protocol notes: pull-up 1RM; back squat velocity @ **½ BW** to hip-crease-below-knee (rope depth), Tendo average concentric m/s; non-CMJ with **1s pause** at depth.

Use as **screens**, not automatic auto-gates - individualize to training age and season.

---

## Quick decision tree

1. Stroke / event + season → volume bias + in-season constraints  
2. Pain? → shoulder menu / PADT (breast) / extension posture before loading more pull  
3. Starts/turns/UW priorities this block? → horizontal/split power + 110-120° + PF/first ray  
4. Always include squat-and-reach + 2 core; add rolling/rotation for free/back  
5. Pair FRC swimmer hovers / HA when end-range ownership is the limiter; pair PRI breathing when ZOA / roll / neck is the limiter

skills.instructions:
---
name: Swim turn and start ISO angles
description: >-
  Use when picking isometric joint angles for swimmers for pool transfer (flip
  turn, open turn, or start) instead of defaulting to a land jump quarter squat.
  Also use when separating CMJ-plate ISO from swim-transfer ISO.
---
# Swim turn and start ISO angles

Locked 2026-09-14 from S&C Research (Araujo 2010; Maglischo; Slawson 2012 OSB11; breast open-turn means).

Swimmers need **turn or start** angles for pool transfer - not a typical land-sport jump depth.

## Two tools (do not mix them up)
1. **CMJ / land plates** → put the ISO where force dips on *their* curve (often ~quarter squat for early bimodal hang).
2. **Pool transfer** → use the turn or start angles below.

Do **not** default every swim ISO to a land quarter squat when the goal is the wall or the block.

## Flip turn (wall push)
- Knee at plant: about **100-120°** (Araujo 2010; Takahashi peak ~120°)
- Hips: about **90°** flexed (Maglischo)
- Too tucked → long wall contact; too straight → weak push

## Open turn (breast / fly)
- Thinner data
- Breast open turns often about **108-112°** knee mean
- Coaching target about **90-120°** knee

## Start (kick / track block)
- Rear knee about **80-90°** for peak vertical force
- Rear knee about **100-110°** for peak horizontal (Slawson 2012 OSB11)
- Many fast starts near about **80°** rear knee
- Keep hips relatively open

## Achieve use
- Breaststroker open-turn ISO ≈ **100-120°** knee
- Freestyle/back flip-turn ISO ≈ **100-120°** knee, hips ~90°
- Start ISO → pick rear-knee band from the intent (more vertical vs more horizontal)
- Name the tool in Direction: plate-dip ISO vs turn/start ISO

Breaststroker example (2026-09-14): plate dip still = quarter-squat `Split Squat ISO Push`; swim-transfer ISO later ≈ 100-120° knee for breast open turn.

# Transcript healthcheck

Scan Grok Bot transcripts on disk for user friction in a time window. Propose new skills, bots, or routines only when evidence supports them. Do not create anything until the user picks a proposal.

## When to run

- the standing `transcript-healthcheck` routine fires
- the user asks for a fleet checkup, friction audit, or "what should we automate"
- first run after this skill is imported (offer cadence then)

## Window and corpus

Default window is the last 24 hours. If a routine or the user names another cadence, use that window instead.

Corpus is on this computer:

- `/home/box/agent-data/agent-transcripts/<agentId>/<agentId>.jsonl`
- skip folders whose names start with `sand-subagent-`
- order candidates by real modification time, never by UUID name
- map `<agentId>` to a name via `/home/box/agent-data/agents/<agentId>/profile.json`

State the window and bot count back before mining.

## How to mine (recall-shaped)

Fan out parallel subagents. Each gets a slice of agent transcript paths. The main thread keeps only their findings.

Each subagent returns one block per bot that had user traffic in the window:

- bot name and id
- user goals in the window (short)
- friction signals with short quotes or paraphrases (cite approx turn or timestamp if present)
- repeated corrections or re-asks
- misunderstandings (bot did X, user wanted Y)
- candidate gaps: skill / bot / routine, one line each, or `none`

Friction to look for:

- frustration, sarcasm, "stop", "wrong", "i said", "undo", "not what i meant"
- same instruction restated
- user doing work the bot should own
- bot asking preference questions an experiment could settle
- quiet failure (user abandons a thread)

Skip bots with no user messages in the window. Null is a finding.

## Report

Lead with a capsule (at most 5 bullets). Then a short list of proposals, each tagged `skill` | `bot` | `routine`, with the evidence line that earned it. Then "no change" bots in one line if useful.

Stay quiet when the routine fires and there is nothing to propose. Do not send "(no change.)".

Offer to implement only after the user picks. Do not CreateAgent, write skills, or create routines from this report alone.

## First-run cadence

On first import, ask once what cadence they want (default weekday morning). Create or update the standing routine named `transcript-healthcheck` to match. Do not ask again every run.
